Having fashioned a mandala consisting of a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square on one's left side, and having sprinkled that mandala with the *Pāśupatāstra* mantra, [one should worship] in the triangle with "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti" and "Oṃ, obeisance to Akhaṇḍamaṇḍala."

Thus: in the hexagon, "Oṃ, obeisance to the solar orb (sūryamaṇḍala)"; in the circle, "Oṃ, obeisance to the all-pervading orb (sarvatovyāpakamaṇḍala)"; and in the square, [as follows]. In the corners: "Obeisance to the seat of Kāmarūpa (kāmarūpapīṭha)"; in the triangle, "Obeisance to the seat of Pūrṇagiri (pūrṇagiripīṭha)"; in the hexagon, "Oṃ, obeisance to the seat of Jālandhara (jālandharapīṭha)"; in the circle, "Oṃ, obeisance to the seat of Oḍiyāna (uḍiyānapīṭha)."

Having worshipped [the deity] in the square, one should worship the six limbs of the root mantra in the hexagon, the three syllables (kūṭas) of the root mantra in the corners of the triangle, and the complete root mantra in the center; furthermore, one should worship the entire fourfold mandala using the individual and collective syllables. Then:

Having washed the base, which is fashioned from gold or other materials, with the *pāśupatāstra* mantra and having placed it upon the mandala, [one should offer obeisance] over it with: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ maṃ dharmapradadaśakalātmane vahnimaṇḍalāya śrīparadevatāyāḥ kalaśādhārāya namaḥ*.
Having worshipped there, one should worship the ten kalās of Fire in a circular form: 4 *yaṃ* *dhūmrārciṣe namaḥ*;
4 *raṃ* *ūṣmāyai namaḥ*; 4 *laṃ* *jvalinyai namaḥ*; 4 *vaṃ* *jvālinyai namaḥ*;
4 *śaṃ* *visphuliṅginyai namaḥ*; 4 *ṣaṃ* *suśriyai namaḥ*; 4 *saṃ* *surūpāyai namaḥ*.

Having worshipped with "Haṃ, obeisance to Kapilā" (four times), "Laṃ, obeisance to Havyavahā" (four times), and "Kṣaṃ, obeisance to Kavyavahā," and having meditated according to the method: "The red-colored digits of Agni, who grant righteousness, hold the gestures of fearlessness and boon-granting," one should invoke the digits of Fire in sequence, saying: "O digits of Fire, come, come here! [Then recite: "The vital breaths of the digits of Fire are here..."

Having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breaths) for them by means of the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā-vidyā* applied to the position of the word "amūṣya" at the beginning of the mantra starting with "prāṇā," one should place upon them a jar made of gold or other materials, possessing auspicious marks, with its neck wrapped in red cloth, smeared with red sandalwood paste, and washed with the *pāśupatāstra-mantra*.

Having established [the vessel] there with "4 Aṃ, obeisance to the jar of the Śrī Paradevatā, which is the solar orb consisting of twelve digits that bestow wealth," one should worship the twelve digits of the Sun in a circular form: "4 Kaṃ Bhaṃ, obeisance to Tapinī; 4 Khaṃ Baṃ, obeisance to Tāpinī; 4..."

Gaṃ Phaṃ, salutation to Dhūmrā; 4 Ghaṃ Paṃ, salutation to Marīci; 4 Ṅaṃ Naṃ, salutation to Jvālinī; 4 Caṃ Dhaṃ, salutation to Ruci; 4 Chaṃ Daṃ, salutation to Suṣumnā; 4 Jaṃ Thaṃ, salutation to Bhogadā; 4 Jhaṃ Taṃ, salutation to Viśvā; Aṃ Ṇaṃ, salutation to Bodhinī; 4.

Having worshipped with "Ṭaṃḍhaṃ Dhāriṇyai namaḥ" (4) and "Ṭhaṃḍaṃ Kṣamāyai namaḥ," and having meditated according to the method: "The digits (kalās), yellow in color, holding the gestures of granting fearlessness and boons, belonging to the Sun, and bestowing wealth," one should perform the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* for them as before, and [install] within that [the mantra] accompanied by the reverse-order Mātṛkā.

Reciting the root-vidyā, fill [the vessel] with pure water and worship it, saying: "Oṃ, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala consisting of sixteen digits that bestows desires, which is the nectar-pitcher of the Śrī Paradevatā. Then, one should worship the sixteen digits of the Moon in a circular form: "Oṃ, obeisance to Amṛtā"; "Oṃ, obeisance to Mānadā."

Namaḥ 4 iṃ Pūṣāyai namaḥ 4 īṃ Tuṣṭyai namaḥ 4 uṃ Puṣṭyai namaḥ 4 ūṃ Ratyai namaḥ 4 ṛṃ Dhṛtyai namaḥ 4 ṝṃ Śaśinyai namaḥ 4 ḷṃ Candrikāyai namaḥ 4 ḹṃ Kāntyai namaḥ 4 eṃ Jyotsnāyai namaḥ 4 aiṃ Śriyai namaḥ 4 oṃ.
Having worshipped with "Salutation to Prīti" (4), "Oṃ, salutation to Aṅgadā" (4), "Aṃ, salutation to Pūrṇā" (4), and "Aḥ,

salutation to Pūrṇāmṛtā," one should meditate upon those digits (kalās) in sequence as being white, gentle, bestowers of desires, and holding the gestures of granting fearlessness and boons; then, as before, perform the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (invocation of the vital breaths) for them.

Having prepared that [mandala], one should place within it unbroken earth from a place where an elephant, horse, or cart has passed, from an anthill, from a confluence, from a lake, and from a cow-pen;
as well as gold, cow-dung, wheat, dūrvā grass, yellow orpiment, and all medicinal herbs. Then, [one offers] to Agni.

Having worshipped within that water with the following: "Oṃ *namaḥ* 4 to Brahmā; *namaḥ* 4 to Bhavānī; *namaḥ* 4 to Gajavaktra; *namaḥ* 4 to Mahoraga; *namaḥ* 4 to Skanda; *namaḥ* 4 to Bhānu; *namaḥ* 4 to the hosts of Mothers; *namaḥ* 4 to the guardians of the directions; *namaḥ* 4 to the nine planets," one should [worship] in its center.

Having placed the eight fragrances there, [one should worship] Varuṇa with the mantra "Vaṃ, obeisance to Varuṇa" using the five offerings, [reciting]: "All oceans, rivers, lakes, streams, and ponds..."
May they come, bringing about the destruction of the sacrificer's misfortunes. || 1 ||

Thus, having summoned the sacred waters with the *kroṃ* syllable and the goad-mudrā (*aṅkuśamudrā*), [one recites]: "O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī—be present in these waters! (1)

Having thus displayed the mudrās beginning with the invocation (āvāhana) and ending with the supreme transformation (paramīkaraṇa), one should gaze at [the vessel] with the root mantra, sprinkle it with water while reciting the weapon mantra (astra), strike it three times with *kuśa* grass using that same mantra, veil it with the armor mantra (kavaca), transform it into nectar by means of the *dhenu-mudrā* while reciting "vaṃ," and then place five sprouts into its mouth.
Viṣṇu is at the mouth of the jar, Rudra is stationed at its neck;
Brahmā is situated at its base, and the hosts of Mothers are stationed in the middle. || 1 ||
Within his belly were all the oceans and the earth with its seven continents;
likewise, the Ṛgveda, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda, and Atharvaveda.
"Accompanied by all their limbs, they are all seated within the pitcher.

Having meditated thus, one should place upon it the vessel for the lid together with the *uddharaṇī*, and cover it with a fine cloth. This is the procedure for the installation of the pitcher of pure water.

(p. 169) Here, the procedure for the placement of the milk jar (*kṣīrakalaśa*) should be understood as being exactly like the placement of the jar of pure water (*śuddhodakakalaśa*). Then, having taken four vessels for the female messengers (*dūtī*), one goes to the house of the *kula* and, having performed the ritual worship of the messengers there according to the rules, [one places] the substance known as *kuṇḍagola* produced therein, secretly, into each individual vessel.

Having done so, one should bring it and place it before oneself; then, having placed each of the four [substances] beginning with *ādya* separately into four vessels, one should perform the consecration (*saṃskāra*) of the five substances contained in the five vessels. It is as follows:
Therein, first is the consecration of the first [vessel]:
"The one supreme Brahman alone, which consists of the gross and the subtle and is eternal—by that, I destroy for you the sin of killing a Brahmin arising from the *kaca* [hair]. (1)
O Goddess, born from the solar disc, arisen from the abode of Varuṇa,
composed of the seed-syllable *amā*, may [this person] be liberated from the curse of Śukra.
If the *praṇava* is the seed of the Vedas and consists of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Goddess, may my sin of killing a Brahmin be removed. (3)

Oṃ 4 vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vaiṃ vauṃ vaḥ, obeisance to the Goddess Sudhā, who releases one from the curse of Brahmā; thus one should recite this ten times over that [substance]. 4 hrīṃ śrīṃ krāṃ krīṃ krūṃ kraiṃ krauṃ kraḥ, release [me] from the curse of Brahmā, [cause] nectar to flow, flow, svāhā; thus one should recite this ten times.
Then, one should recite the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*) over it eight times; this is the first purification. Now follows the second purification:
4. *Oṃ prātardviṣṇuḥ stavate vīryeṇa mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ | yasyoruṣu triṣu vikramaṇeṣvadhikṣayanti bhuvanāni viśvā ||* 4. *Oṃ tatpuruṣāya vidmahe...*

"Let us meditate upon Mahādeva; may Rudra impel us. Having recited this ten times over that [object], one should also recite the root-vidyā ten times. This is the second purification. Now, the third purification: *Oṃ, we worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity, like a cucumber [from its stem]...*

"May I be released from bondage, death, and non-immortality"—having recited this ten times over that [object], one should also recite the root mantra ten times; this is the third purification. Now, the fourth purification:
[one should visualize] a wholesome *kṛsara* (rice and sesame) in the form of a mandala, resembling the orb of the moon.
And a charming caru, filled with sugar and other such ingredients. || 1 ||
This mudrā is proclaimed for the deity at the time of worship.
Its purification is as follows: *Oṃ tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ | divīva cakṣur ātatam || tad viprāso vipanyavo jāgṛvāṃsaḥ samindhate*.

"Viṣṇu’s supreme abode. Having thus recited [the mantra] ten times over that, one should also recite the root-vidyā ten times; this is the fourth purification. Now, the fifth purification: *Oṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavarṣiṇi, release the curse of Śukra, cause nectar to flow, cause it to flow.*

Reciting "amṛtaṃ kuru kuru svāhā" over it ten times, one should also recite the root-mantra (mūlavidyā) ten times; this is the fifth purification. Having thus generally purified the five substances and placed them in vessels such as jars, one should purify them specifically for a second time. Then, at the conclusion of the worship of the Goddess—
At the time of self-surrender, one should perform the surrender after purifying oneself for the third time;
and that [method] is to be understood from the mouth of the venerable Guru.
As it is said in the Kulārṇava:
Fermented liquor, meat, fish, mudrā,
and beef— these five substances one should then purify in three ways.
"O Goddess, they are not purified otherwise, unless what has been declared is followed.

This means that if the threefold purification is not performed, then—as stated in the Śruti, Smṛti, Purāṇas, and so forth—the aforementioned defect resulting from contact with these five substances occurs; that is, it is incurred.

The ritual procedure for the offering to the messenger (dūtīyāga) should be understood from the *Sthūlapaddhati* and other such works. The purification of the self-originated [liṅga] (*svayambhū*) is to be known as being like the purification of that which arises from a cow (*golottha*). Now, regarding the purification of the commitments (*samaya*), it is said in the *Kulārṇava*:
"Between consciousness (*saṃvit*) and the wine of the sacrificial drink (*āsava*), consciousness alone is more important."
The application of consciousness should be performed by the best of practitioners at the beginning of worship and other rites. || 1 ||
"And a great worship must be performed by those who are well-resolved.

This practice is to be performed everywhere at the beginning of worship and other rites by those of noble family (*kulīna*). Furthermore, elsewhere it is said: "Without bliss there is ruin, and the deities are not satisfied. And she [the consort] may be a Brāhmaṇī, a Kṣatriyā, or a Vaiśyā.
The Śūdrās are of four kinds, distinguished by white, red, yellow, and black flowers. Regarding their purification: O Consciousness, born of Brahman, daughter of Brahman, eternally sinless!
For the sake of the satisfaction of the Bhairavas, be forever pure. (1)
Reciting "Oṃ brāhmayai namaḥ svāhā" ten times over that [vessel], and then reciting the root mantra eight times, constitutes the purification of the Brāhmī vessel.

O Goddess, who brings about the root of accomplishment, who awakens the fundamental enlightenment, who brings the sons of kings under control, and who wields the trident against the throats of enemies! (1)
Having recited "Aiṃ, obeisance to Kṣatriyā, Svāhā" ten times, one should also recite the root mantra eight times;
thus is the purification of the Kṣatriyā.
O lamp at the tip of the fuel of ignorance, O flame of knowledge, O you whose form is knowledge—considering this offering of bliss and the rest, grant me perfect knowledge. || 1 ||
Having recited "hrīṃ vaiśyāyai namaḥ svāhā" ten times, one should also recite the root mantra eight times;
this is the purification of the Vaiśyā.
I pay homage, I pay homage to you, O Mother who reveals the path of yoga! O Conqueror of the Three Worlds, grant me the fruit of meditative absorption. (1)

Having recited "Śrīṃ, obeisance to Śūdrā, Svāhā" ten times, one should recite the root mantra eight times; this is the purification of the pure and impure. Now, the general method for purifying all [the vessels] is as follows: having gazed at them with the root mantra and sprinkled them with the Astra mantra, one should strike them three times with Kuśa grass, Dūrvā grass, or similar items using that same mantra.

Having veiled it with the *kavaca* mantra and rendered it nectarine with "Vam," [recite] four times: "Oṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtam ākarṣaya tvaṃ siddhiṃ dehi svāhā. Having recited this ten times over it, one should recite the root mantra eight times. Then, having displayed the ten mudrās beginning with the invocation (*āvāhana*) above that—
Having performed the ritual placement of the vase (*kalaśa-sthāpana*)— just as in the case of placing the vase of pure water— and having filled it with *vijayāmṛta*,
one should perform all the rites such as the worship of the wheel-assembly (*cakrakalā-pūjā*) exactly as in the procedure for placing the vase of pure water;
then, preceded by the binding of the directions (*digbandha*), a snap of the fingers (*cchoṭikā*), and three claps of the hands (*tāla*).

Having dispelled the obstacles lurking in the netherworld, the earth, and the sky by striking the heels together, clapping the hands, and raising the face upward, and having offered libations seven times into the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) with the root mantra,
[one should worship] the venerable Guru residing in the center of the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus by means of the *saṅketa-vidyā*.

At the end of the Śrīgurupādukā-vidyā, having offered libations three times with the words "I satisfy the Śrīgurupādukā," and at the end of the Mūla-mantra, having satisfied the Mūladevī three times with the Tattvamudrā while reciting "I satisfy the Śrīparadevatā," [one recites]: "Mūla: Aiṃ vadavada vāgvādini, be firmly established on the tip of my tongue."

Reciting the mantra *sarvasattvavaśaṅkari svāhā*, one should personally consume the *vijayāmṛta* (the nectar of victory) taken from the flask through another vessel; then, covering it with the lifting-vessel placed upon the flask, one should cover all of that with a fine cloth. This is the procedure for the installation of the *vijayā* flask.
Now, regarding the substitute substances, the Kulārṇava states:
"In the absence of the primary [substance], one should worship after mixing a *vaṭaka* (ball of food) with water;
or the wise practitioner, having taken a *vaṭaka* mixed with buttermilk..."
One should perform this rite with buttermilk mixed with jaggery, or with that same [buttermilk] combined with honey, or else with *sauvīra*; one must not omit this action.
In the absence of the second [substance], one should place garlic, fresh ginger, or dry ginger and worship the Goddess; otherwise, it shall be fruitless.
Thus, in the Vīratantra: "O Maheśānī, the five—salt, fresh ginger, oil-cake, wheat, and black gram—as well as garlic, are prescribed as the second substitute. (1)
"But in the absence of the third [flower] and those following, one should indeed employ this very [substitute].

There is no substitute for the fourth and so forth; however, as for the substitute for the fifth and so forth, having brought Aparājitā flowers and Hayāri flowers, one should fill the Aparājitā flower with sandalwood and other substances.
Having joined the *hayāri* flower with that [other] one there, having contemplated both as the union of Śiva and Śakti,

and having visualized the arising of the *kula* substance, one should mutter one's own *vidyā* over them according to one's capacity and then cast those two flowers into the center of the special *arghya*. Other [flowers] as well...
Substitute materials such as milk and the like should be employed according to one's specific eligibility. Now, following the tradition of the Kālīmata, the general *arghya* vessel is established:
there, to the front-left of oneself, a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, and a square is drawn with sandalwood paste and other substances.
Having fashioned that maṇḍala with dust or water using whatever materials are available, and having sprinkled it with the *pāśupatāstra* mantra, one should worship as follows:

in the center of the triangle, say "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti"; likewise in the three corners, in the circle, and in the square, say "Oṃ, obeisance to Akhaṇḍamaṇḍala" and "Oṃ, obeisance to Pūrṇamaṇḍala. Oṃ...

Having worshipped the maṇḍala with the mantra "Obeisance to the all-pervading maṇḍala," one should wash the vessel (ādhāra) made of gold or other materials with the Pāśupata-weapon mantra (astra), place it upon the maṇḍala, and [worship] the fire-maṇḍala consisting of ten kalās that bestows dharma, for the sake of the Śrī Parādevatā.

Having worshipped the conch-base with "Oṃ, obeisance to the conch-base (śaṅkhādhāra)," and having meditated upon the base as being of the nature of fire, one should again wash the conch with the Pāśupata-weapon mantra and place it upon the base. Then [one worships] with:
"Oṃ, to the solar disc consisting of twelve kalās that bestows wealth, for the sake of the Śrī Paradevatā..."

Having worshipped the conch with "Obeisance to Śaṅkhapātra" and meditated upon the conch as having the form of the Sun, one should fill the conch three-quarters full with pure water while reciting the *viloma-mātṛkā* (the reverse alphabet) together with the root mantra and the daily *nityā-vidyā* of that day, leaving one part remaining for the purpose of the special filling (*viśeṣapūraṇa*).

Then, having worshipped within the water with the mantra: "Oṃ, obeisance to the nectar of the conch of the Śrī Parādevatā, for the lunar maṇḍala whose self consists of the sixteen digits that grant desires," one should contemplate that water as being the form of the Moon,
and [place] fragrant flowers, unbroken rice, barley, tips of kuśa grass, sesame seeds, white mustard, curd, dūrvā grass, and so forth, into the water in the conch.

"O Ravi, by the truth that whatever holy places (*tīrthas*) exist upon the earth have been touched by your hand—by that truth, O God, O Maker of Day, grant me a holy place. Having thus drawn forth the holy waters from the solar orb with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* and placed them into the water of the conch, [he recites] "O Gaṅgā and Yamunā... and so forth.

Having invoked the sacred sites (tīrthas) and displayed the ten mudrās beginning with the invocation (āvāhana), having worshipped them with the five offerings (pañcopacāra), having displayed the Gālinī mudrā while uttering "vaṣaṭ," having gazed [at them] while uttering "vauṣaṭ," and having veiled [them] while uttering "huṃ," [one should perform this] in the southeast, northeast, southwest, northwest, and in the center, as well as in the cardinal directions, with the root mantra (mūlavidyā).

Having worshipped the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) and likewise displayed the six-limbed mudrās (*ṣaḍaṅgamudrā*), one should place the right thumb into the water, cover it with the fish-mudrā (*matsyamudrā*), and while touching the water, recite the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*) eight times. Then,
having protected it with the *pāśupatāstra* using the arrow-mudrā (*nārācamudrā*), [one should utter] "Vam."

Having rendered [the water] nectar-like by means of the *dhenumudrā*, having displayed the *yonimudrā* with "Aiṃ," the *śaṅkhamudrā* with "Śrīṃ," the *cakramudrā* with "Phaṭ," and the *paramīkaraṇamudrā* with "Hrīṃ," one should contemplate that water as consisting of radiant light. This is the installation of the conch (*śaṅkhasthāpana*). Here, according to the *Kādimata*:
I shall describe later the method for placing the primary jar (*pradhānakalaśa*), the general vessels (*sāmānyapātra*), and the specific vessels (*viśeṣapātra*);

I shall also explain the placement of the *śrīpātra*. As for the placement of the vessels beginning with the *śakti*, it is exactly like that of the general vessel; the only difference is that one should offer a drop of special *arghya* while reciting the respective mantra.
One should recite [the mantra] ten times for each of the ten [vessels]. The vessel of Śakti [is consecrated] with the Bālā [mantra];

the vessel of the Guru with the Gurupādukā-vidyā; the vessel of enjoyment (bhoga-pātra) with the Samaṣṭi-vidyā; the consecration of all the vessels of the sacrificial offering (bali-pātra) with the mantras of their respective deities; and the limb-vessel (aṅga-pātra).
One should consecrate the hero’s vessel with the mantras of the six-limbed maiden, the secret vessel with the Kāmarāja mantra,
the yoginī’s vessel with the Navacakreśvarī vidyās,
one’s own vessel once each with the eight-syllable mantra of the self, and the sprinkling vessel with the same.

One should consecrate the four vessels for the female messengers (*dūtī*) with the root-mantras and the six ancillary mantras (*ṣaḍaṅga*), using the *bālā* mantra. As it is stated in the venerable *Kulārṇava*:
"O lady of excellent hips, the wise practitioner should recite the mantra over the vessel of the *śakti* ten times."
Covering the young maiden Tripureśvarī with his right hand.
In the same way, O Śivā, the vessel of the Guru is consecrated with the Pādukā-vidyā;
O Goddess, the vessel for enjoyment is consecrated with the Samaṣṭi-vidyā.
O Sovereign of the Gods,
with the six-limbed *yuvatī* mantras, one should sprinkle the vessel for the limbs and the vessels for the *bali* deities once each, O Sureśvarī.
O Great Goddess, O observer of excellent vows, the Hero’s Vessel is [consecrated] by Kāmarāja;
but the Secret Vessel, O Supreme Goddess, is [consecrated] by the seed-syllable of Kuṇḍalī.
O Ambikā, the vessel for the Yoginīs is [prepared] by the nine Mistress-of-the-Circle goddesses;
O Maheśvarī, the vessel for oneself is prepared with the eight-syllable mantra of the Self.

O Adrijā, O Maheśānī, one should sprinkle the *prokṣaṇī* vessel with the mantras of the six limbs of knowledge (*vidyā-ṣaḍaṅga*), and likewise, O Kūmārī, the four vessels for the female messengers (*dūtī*).
Such authoritative statements (pramāṇavacanāni) as these, spoken in various tantras, are to be understood.

Likewise, the consecration (abhimantraṇa) of the five vessels, beginning with the *arghya*, by means of the mantras consisting of the respective deities is also to be understood. As for that which says: "Having prepared the *arghya* with the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) and root mantras, one should worship according to the rule."

This sequence, beginning with "ityādi," should be understood as the procedure for the abbreviated worship (*saṃkṣepapūjā*). That sequence is as follows: having drawn the mandala as before and worshipped it there with unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), one should place the washed support (*ādhāra*) there, contemplate it as being of the nature of fire, and then place upon it the vessel containing the *arghya* and other offerings, which have been washed with the weapon-mantra (*astra*).

Having meditated upon the form of the Sun and worshipped it, one should fill [the vessel] with water while reciting the *mātṛkā* in reverse order together with the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*). Having meditated upon that water as the form of the Moon and worshipped it, one should sequentially pour into it the five purified substances, each separately, into the five vessels as previously described.

Having worshipped with unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) ten times using the six-limbed mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*) in the sequence beginning with the directions of Agni, Īśāna, Asura, Vāyu, and the center, one should recite the third *kūṭa* of Śrīvidyā ten times, and elsewhere the respective mantras of those deities ten times; then, one should contemplate that water as being of the nature of light (*tejas*). Thus it is stated in the Kādimata.
In brief, this is the setting out of the vessels.

One should accomplish the *arghya* offering by means of the recitation and worship performed ten times with the third *kūṭa* of the *vidyā* and the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) of the Root Goddess, and then perform the worship.

Thus, according to the statement from the *Kādimata*: "In reality, however, this is an emergency procedure (*āpatkalpa*); an emergency procedure is censured in the case of the primary ritual (*mukhyapūjā*), for there the primary procedure (*mukhyakalpa*) alone is more excellent."
In the worship of the Kumārī, the consecration (abhimantraṇa) of the five vessels, beginning with the arghya vessel, is performed with the Bāla-mantra;

however, in the procedure for the worship of the garland, it is performed with the Prāsāda-mantra. In the worship of the seed-syllables (akṣara) and medicinal herbs, it is done with the mantras of the five elements (pañcabhūta); likewise, in the worship of the five deities (pañcāyatana), each respective vessel is consecrated with its own specific mantra.

In the worship of the fifty couples, one should use the Mātṛkā; in the worship of the elemental deities, the Bhairavī; in the ritual of Kālanityā, the specific Nityā-vidyā of that particular day; in the worship of the book, the Prāsāda mantra alone; in the worship of the fire, its own specific mantra; and in the rites of worship and so forth for married couples, young women, and Yoginīs.

One should perform the consecration (*abhimantraṇa*) with the *bālaya* mantra. For the lifting and covering [of the vessel], there is washing with the *pāśupatāstra* mantra and the consecration at that very spot. For the vessels containing edible items such as the food offering (*naivedya*), [the consecration is performed] with the weapon-mantra (*astramantra*) taught in the six-limbed mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*) of the respective deities' root-mantras.
The washing and the consecration (*abhimantraṇa*) with that [same substance]— all this, having learned from the guru and from the scriptures,
should be applied in the ritual worship.
[This applies to substances] produced from the powder of *nārava*, *vaiśvāmitra*, *akṣara*, and medicinal herbs, or from mantras, constellations, trees, and similar wombs (*yoni*).

The purification (*saṃskāra*) of the vessels should be understood according to the same method of brief ritual procedure previously described, as there is no purpose in performing an abundance of purifications for them. The purification of the perfected substances (*siddhadravya*) must be performed every day; a substance purified on one day is censured for use in worship on another day.
However, for the *svayambhūkusuma* that has already been consecrated, there is no further consecration on another day. As it is said in the *Kulārṇava*:
"The preceptor, having thoroughly purified the *svayambhūkusuma*..."
With that [flower], one should perform the worship of the Goddess and the ritual closing of the eyes. || 1 ||
By that, the Great Goddess is pleased and bestows all accomplishments (*siddhi*).
Furthermore, the wise one should purify other substances of accomplishment every day. (2)

On one day a substance may be pure, while on another it may be censurable; by this it is meant that for daily worship, fresh substances—excluding *svayambhū* flowers—that have been proven effective are recommended. Now, regarding the purification of the substance for drawing the yantra: therein—
Having placed the eight substances— musk, agallochum, camphor, kuṇḍagolodbhava, kesar, jaggery, sandalwood, and the self-arisen flower— in a single vessel,
one should consecrate them seven times with the Amṛteśvarī and Dīpinī vidyās. As it has been said:
In the Bhairavītantra:
O Great Goddess, [the substances are] musk, agallochum, camphor, and *golottha*; likewise, wild honey, jaggery, sandalwood from Malaya, and the *svayambhū* flower. (1)
Having combined everything together, one should empower the hand by placing it separately seven times over each with the *dīpinī-amṛta-vidyā*.
"By that [process], the substance becomes pure; with that very substance, one should indeed write.
Here, the *golottha* (the substance arising from the *goḷa*) and the *svayambhūkusuma* (spontaneously arisen flower) must be taken as having been purified in a separate vessel, just as before.

Now, the installation of the jar and other vessels according to the Kālīmata: there, having fashioned a mandala to the front-left of oneself— just like the mandala for the special arghya (viśeṣārghya) to be described later— and having worshipped it in the same manner,
one should place the washed support (ādhāra) there according to the procedure to be described, and worship it likewise.

A flask fashioned from gold or other materials, perfumed with incense, is washed with the left hand while reciting *huṃ huṃ brahmāṇḍacaṣakāya svāhā*; it is then ignited with the *Sandīpinī* mantra, *aiṃ sandīpini jvālāmālini hrīṃ*, using the *yonimudrā*,
and veiled with the *kavaca* mantra, *oṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*.

Having performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*) with the five mantras: *namaḥ kṣaṃ*, *namaḥ haṃ*, *namaḥ saḥ*, *namaḥ* [and *namaḥ yaṃ*], and having established the great water-jar (*kalaśa*) there with the words: *oṃ 3 śrīmahātripurasundaryā mahākalaśaṃ sthāpayāmi*, one should worship [the jar] there up to the digit of the Sun (*sūryakalā*), just like the special vessel for the *arghya* offering (*viśeṣārghyapātra*) which will be described later.
Therein, having filled [the vessel] with water that has been well-scented with camphor and other fragrances, stale and strained,
and having placed a lotus or similar object therein, one should visualize within its center the mandala to be described for the special arghya (viśeṣārghya),
and worship up to the lunar digits (somakalā) according to the procedure to be described.
Around that square [mandala], [recite]: *Oṃ 3 hsakhapreṃ pathikadevatābhyo huṃphaṭ svāhā namaḥ*.
*Oṃ 3 hsakhaphreṃ grāmacaṇḍālini huṃphaṭ svāhā namaḥ*. *Oṃ 3 hasakhaphreṃ krodhacaṇḍālini huṃphaṭ svāhā namaḥ*. *Oṃ 3 hasakhaphreṃ dṛṣṭicaṇḍālini*...

Huṃ phaṭ svāhā! Homage! Oṃ 3 ha sa kha phreṃ! O Sparśacaṇḍālinī, huṃ phaṭ svāhā! Homage! Oṃ 3 ha sa kha phreṃ! O Sṛṣṭicaṇḍālinī, huṃ phaṭ svāhā! Homage! Oṃ 3 ha sa kha phreṃ! O Ghaṭacaṇḍālinī, huṃ phaṭ svāhā! Homage! Oṃ 3 ha sa kha phreṃ...
Tapanavedhacaṇḍālini hūṃ phaṭ svāhā namaḥ | oṃ 3 hsakhaphreṃ nindācaṇḍālini hūṃ phaṭ svāhā namaḥ | oṃ 3 hsakhaphreṃ sarvajanadṛṣṭisparśacaṇḍālini hūṃ phaṭ svāhā namaḥ | oṃ 3 hsakhaphreṃ...

"Paśupāśacaṇḍālini hūṃ phaṭ svāhā namaḥ. Thus one should worship, proceeding clockwise starting from the front. Having thus dispelled the ten defects, one should worship in the center of the *hetu* with: "Oṃ 3 kāṃ kīṃ kūṃ kaiṃ kauṃ kaḥ, O Drier of Transformations (*vikāraśoṣiṇi*), destroy, destroy the transformations of this [person], svāhā!"
He is extended by the five preceding verses beginning with "svādiṣṭhayā," by the three [verses] beginning with "viṣṇuryoniṃ," and by the triad beginning with "tribhiṣṭvā. || 1 ||
One should release the curse of Śukra by means of the two verses beginning with "imaṃ me," with the one verse beginning with "tā mande," and with the one verse beginning with "śroṇāmekā. || 2 ||

Thus, according to the statement of the *Kulārṇava*, one should consecrate [the substance] once with each of the fifteen mantras mentioned. As for those mantras, they are as follows from the *Ṛgveda*: "Flow on, O Soma, with your most sweet and most intoxicating stream, pressed for Indra to drink. (1)
The slayer of demons, the observer of all people, has settled upon his seat with the wooden vessel, having reached the womb that bestows vigor.
Be most wide-reaching, most bountiful, and the greatest slayer of Vṛtra; bring across the wealth of our patrons. 3.
Flow toward the banquet of the great gods with the exhilarating juice; flow toward strength and fame. 4.
Toward you we move, for this very purpose day after day; O Indu, upon you alone are our hopes.
May Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms;
may Prajāpati pour [the seed]; may Dhātṛ place the embryo within you.
Bestow the embryo, O Sinīvālī; bestow the embryo, O Sarasvatī.
May the two divine Aśvins, adorned with lotus-garlands, place the embryo within you. 2.
That which the Aśvins churn with the two golden fire-sticks—
that embryo of yours we invoke, so that you may bring it forth in the tenth month. (10.184.1–3) O God Savitṛ, with your three most excellent Soma-abodes...
O Agni, purify us with your powers of skill. || 1 ||
May the divine beings purify me; may the Vasus purify me with their wisdom.
O Viśvedevas, purify me; O Jātavedas, purify me.
Flow forth, O Soma, pour yourself out with all your rays;
you are the most excellent oblation for the gods. (9.67.6–28, p.
173) O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, and Paruṣṇī, accept this my hymn of praise!
By the Asiknī, by the Marudvr̥dhā, by the Vitastā, by the Arjīkīyā, and by the Suṣomā, hear [me]!
(10.75.5) Where the white and black rivers meet, those who, having crossed over, fly up toward heaven—those wise men who indeed cast off their bodies, they partake in immortality. (10.40.13)

Rejoicing in the dwelling of man, bestow upon the seeker wealth together with heroic sons. O Lords of Splendor, create a ford that is easy to traverse; strike down the obstacle standing in the path and destroy evil intent.
One drives the cow to the water at Śroṇā; one skins the meat brought on the butcher’s block for a month;
one carries away the dung as far as the slope. What indeed did the two parents do for their sons? (4) (1.16).
Having thus consecrated [the food] with "Oṃ 3 hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ vūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ amṛte amṛtādbhave..."

O Amṛteśvarī, O showerer of nectar, O you whose nature is nectar, cause the nectar to flow, flow! Release the nectar from the curse of Śukra; salutation to Mocikā! Having consecrated [the substance] eight times with this mantra—*oṃ 3 jūṃ saḥ svāhā*—[one should then recite]: *oṃ 3 siddhāyai namaḥ*, *oṃ 3 raktāyai namaḥ*, *oṃ 3*.

Having worshipped in clockwise order, starting from one's own front, in the four directions of the square with "Oṃ 3, obeisance to Śuklā" and "Oṃ 3, obeisance to Utpalā," one should visualize the central triangle as the special *arghya* (offering water) of the form to be described,
and [offer] "Oṃ 3 hasakṣamalavarayūṃ, vauṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava."

I worship the sandals of Ānandabhairava; I satiate them; salutations! Oṃ 3 sahakṣamalavarayīṃ, vaṣaṭ to Ānandabhairavī; I worship the sandals of Ānandabhairavī; I satiate them; salutations! Thus everywhere. Oṃ 3, vauṣaṭ to Surānandabhairava. Oṃ.
Oṃ 3 Surānandabhairavyai Vaṣaṭ; Surānandabhairavī-Śrī. Oṃ 3 Amṛtānandabhairavāya;
Oṃ 3 Amṛtānandabhairavyai. Oṃ 3 Taruṇānandabhairavāya; Oṃ 3 Taruṇānandabhairavyai. Oṃ 3 Unmanānandabhairavāya; Oṃ 3.
To Unmanānanda Bhairavī, Oṃ 3; to Jñānānanda Bhairava, Oṃ 3; to Jñānānanda Bhairavī, Oṃ 3; to Muktyānanda Bhairava, Oṃ 3;
to Muktyānanda Bhairavī, Oṃ 3; to Paramānanda Bhairava, Oṃ 3.
Having worshipped and gratified the nine Bhairava couples— *paramānandabhairavyai* Oṃ 3 *kālabhairavāya* Oṃ 3 *kālabhairavyai*— in the center and in the directions,
one should gaze at them with the *vīkṣaṇamudrā* using the root mantra, sprinkle them with water using the *astramantra*, and [sweep] with *kuśa* grass using the *astramantra*.
Having struck [the water] with the armor-mantra (kavaca-mantra), sprinkled it, and smelled it, one visualizes it entering through the left nostril,
proceeding to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), and merging there into the ocean of supreme nectar situated within the lunar orb of consciousness (cic-candramaṇḍala).
One then contemplates that water emerging from the gap between the upper teeth by way of the eyes, becoming identical with that [nectar].
Having restrained [the deity] with the *saṃrodhana-mudrā*, veiled it with the *avaguṇṭhana-mudrā* using the armor-mantra (*kavaca-mantra*),
rendered it nectar-like with the *dhenu-mudrā* while reciting "vaṃ," and made it supreme with the *paramīkaraṇa-mudrā*, one should meditate upon the Goddess there,
worship her with perfumes, flowers, and so forth, and consecrate her eight times with the root-vidyā: Oṃ 3.

Homage to the Blessed One, Māheśvarī, whose form is the water of Vāruṇī; O you who seize the upward-pointing drop, Sovereign Lady Mahālakṣmī, in the supreme abode, radiant in the supreme ether, devourer of the moon, sun, and fire!
Come, come! Enter, enter! Take, take the substances for your own enjoyment! Svāhā!

At that time, taking a drop from the flask with the thumb and ring finger of the left hand using the second fragment held [there], one should cast it upward. Then, having covered the mouth of the flask with another vessel, one should take the vessel for removal, place it in the left hand, and [recite] "Oṃ 3 Amoghāyai."

Having worshipped the four powers (śakticatuṣṭaya) with "Oṃ 3, obeisance to Sūkṣmā; Oṃ 3, obeisance to Ānandā; Oṃ 3, obeisance to Śāntī," in the vessel placed in the left hand, one should place it upon the covering vessel of the pitcher; thus having performed the ritual installation of the pitcher (kalaśasthāpana), then—
On the southern side of the *kalaśa*, having fashioned a mandala consisting of a square, a circle,
and a triangle on ground smeared with sandalwood paste and other substances while reciting the three *tāras* through the path of the right nostril,
one should worship the center of the triangle with the root mantra preceded by the *praṇava* and the three *tāras* and ending with *namaḥ*.

Having worshipped the three corners of the triangle by means of the three *kūṭas* in a clockwise direction starting from one's own front, and having worshipped the four limbs beginning with the Heart in the corners of the square— namely Agni, Īśāna, Nirṛti, and Vāyu— and the Eye in the center and the Weapon in the four directions starting from the East, using the six limb-mantras (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*), [one should worship] there with the Root-mantra (*mūla*).
Having washed and placed the base vessel (*ādhāra*), one should utter the first *kūṭa*—*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*—and worship it with:
*raṃ vahnimaṇḍalāya dharmapradadaśakalātmane śrīparadevatāyāḥ sāmānyārghyādhārāya namaḥ*. (Therein, according to the method to be described...)

Having worshipped the ten digits (kalās) of Fire, one should place the vessel washed there with the Astra-mantra and, having uttered the second Kūṭa— *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*— [offer it] to the general *arghya* vessel of the Śrī Parādevatā, [dedicated to] the Sun-maṇḍala, whose self consists of the twelve digits that bestow wealth (*arthaprada*), with the mantra: *aṃ*.

Having worshipped the vessel with "Namaḥ," one should worship the twelve kalās of the Sun therein according to the method to be described hereafter. Then, filling that vessel with pure water scented with perfumes such as sandalwood paste while reciting the Mātṛkā in reverse order at the end of the Praṇava, the three Tāras, and the Mūlavidyā, one should utter "Oṃ" three times and the third Kūṭa, "Oṃ."

Having worshipped the water with the mantra: "Obeisance to the Soma-maṇḍala, the essence of the sixteen digits that bestows desires, the nectar of the general offering (sāmānyārghya) of the venerable Supreme Deity," according to the method to be described hereafter.

Having worshipped the sixteen digits (kalās) of Soma there as before, having invoked the sacred water (tīrtha) from the solar disc (savitṛmaṇḍala), and having offered a drop of nectar (amṛtabindu) from the jar, one should place perfumes, flowers, and so forth there with the root mantra.
Then, having worshipped it with the six-limbed mantras (ṣaḍaṅgamantra) as before, [one recites]: *hasakṣamalavarayūṃ sahakṣamalavarayīṃ*.
Having consecrated it three times with the Navātma-mithuna mantra, and having likewise consecrated it three times with the Varuṇa-mithuna mantra— *hasauṃ varuṇāya namaḥ, śauṃ vāruṇīdevyai namaḥ*—
and having consecrated it eight times with the root mantra (*mūla*), one should display the Dhenu and Yoni mudrās; this is the general *arghya*.

Having prepared that area by smearing the ground with ordinary *argha* water mixed with fragrant substances such as *yakṣakardama*, one should construct there a mandala consisting of a square, a circle, a hexagon, and a triangle, using the upward-flowing breaths of the two nostrils; then, that mandala—

Having grasped [the vessel] with the left hand marked by the conch mudrā, one should draw the *kāmakalā*—which has the nature of the fourth state (*turya*) together with the *bindu*—in the center of the triangle therein, and then [worship] the mandala with: "Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the mandala that is the support for the special arghya of the Supreme Deity. Thus [one worships] the mandala.
Having worshipped with the root mantra ending in *namaḥ* four times, and having worshipped the center of the triangle, one should worship the triangle in a clockwise direction:
at the front corner of the triangle, "4 [mantra] first kūṭa, *namaḥ*"; on the left, "4 second [kūṭa], *namaḥ*"; on the right, "4 third [kūṭa], *namaḥ*".
Then, in the corners of the hexagon, proceeding clockwise...

Having worshipped the three root-peaks (*mūlakūṭa*) twice, starting from their own apex (*svāgra*), and having worshipped the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) in the square as before, one should worship within that square— in the four directions starting from the own-apex and in the center— proceeding clockwise with: *4 glūṃ gaganaratnāya namaḥ*, *4 slūṃ svargaratnāya namaḥ*, *4 mlūṃ*.

"Oṃ martyaratnāya namaḥ 4; plūṃ pātālaratnāya namaḥ 4; nlūṃ nāgaratnāya namaḥ 4"—having thus worshipped the five jewels (*pañcaratna*), one should again worship the six seats mentioned in the ritual of placement (*nyāsa*) within the hexagons, proceeding clockwise starting from the eastern point. [Then] in the square, the circle, the hexagon, and the triangle... 4.
"Salutation to Kāmarūpa-pīṭha," "Salutation to Jālandhara-pīṭha," "Salutation to Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha," "Salutation to Uḍḍiyāna-pīṭha"— having thus worshipped the four seats (pīṭhas),
if one possesses the Śāmbhava initiation, [one should worship] within the square at the four directions starting from one's own front and in the center.

One should perform worship with five sets of *praṇavas* encapsulated by five *praṇavas*. It is as follows: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasakhaphreṃ hasauḥ aiṃ hasauḥ hasakhaphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ namaḥ*. Likewise: *hrīṃ 5 namaḥ*, *śrīṃ 5 namaḥ*, *hasakhaphreṃ 5 namaḥ*, *hasauḥ 5 namaḥ*.

One should worship. Then, having worshipped the entire mandala with the root mantra: "Obeisance to the arghya-maṇḍala consisting of the four seats of the Śrī Paradevatā, who is composed of all powers," one should take the base (ādhāra) washed there with the root mantra and [offer it] to the Śrī Paradevatā.
Thinking, "I shall establish the support for the special arghya," he places it upon the mandala;

having uttered the first *kūṭa* and recited, "Oṃ, salutation to the support of the special arghya vessel of the venerable Supreme Deity, whose self consists of the ten kalās that bestow dharma, belonging to the fire-mandala (*vahnimaṇḍala*)," he worships the support.

Above that, having invoked the ten digits of fire—beginning with Dhūmrārcis—with the mantra "Come, come here! (ihāgacchatāgacchata), one should perform the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* for them; therein, using the previously mentioned *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* mantra, one should substitute the word "of me" (*mama*) with "of Dhūmrārcis and the others."

Having placed one's foot [on the disciple] and performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breaths) by reciting the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā-mantra* while touching the base, one should proceed as follows: 4 *Yaṃ* Dhūmrārciṣe namaḥ | 4 *Raṃ* Uṣmāyai namaḥ | 4 *Laṃ* Jvalinyai namaḥ | 4 *Vaṃ* Jvālinyai namaḥ | 4 *Śaṃ* Visphuliṅginyai namaḥ | 4 *Ṣaṃ*...

Having worshipped them with "Suśriye namaḥ" (4), "Saṃ Surūpāyai namaḥ" (4), "Haṃ Kapilāyai namaḥ" (4), "Laṃ Havyavāhāyai namaḥ" (4), and "Kṣaṃ Kavyavāhāyai namaḥ" (4), one should wash a vessel made of gold or other materials with the Astra-mantra and [offer it] to the Supreme Deity. Śrīparadevatāyāḥ...

Having established the special *arghya* vessel there with "I establish the special *arghya* vessel; obeisance," and having uttered the second *kūṭa* four times, one should worship within the vessel with: "Obeisance to the special *arghya* vessel of the venerable Supreme Deity, which is the essence of the twelve digits that bestow wealth and belongs to the solar orb (*arkamaṇḍala*). Thus, having worshipped the vessel in its center.
Having visualized the previously described maṇḍala and having performed worship as before up to the five jewels,

one should likewise honor it with the five *praṇavas*. Then, having invoked the twelve digits (*kalā*) of the Sun there as before, one should perform the ritual installation of their vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) preceded by their respective names, as previously described.
One should worship them in a circular form, proceeding clockwise. Namely: 4 *kaṃ bhaṃ* *tapinyai* namaḥ;
4 *khaṃ baṃ* *tāpinyai* namaḥ; 4 *gaṃ phaṃ* *dhūmrāyai* namaḥ; 4 *ghaṃ paṃ* *marīcyai* namaḥ; 4 *ṅaṃ naṃ* *jvālinyai* namaḥ; 4 *caṃ dhaṃ* *rucyai* namaḥ; 4 *chaṃ daṃ*.
*Suṣumnāyai namaḥ* 4; *Jaṃ thaṃ bhogadāyai namaḥ* 4; *Jhaṃ taṃ viśvāyai namaḥ* 4;

*Ñaṃ ṇaṃ bodhinyai namaḥ* 4; *Ṭaḍhaṃ dhāriṇyai namaḥ* 4; *Ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ kṣamāyai namaḥ* 4. Having thus worshipped, one should draw up the water contained in the pitcher with a vessel for drawing water, at the end of the root mantra (*mūlavidyā*).

Reciting the *mātṛkā* in reverse order, he fills that vessel; having placed a lotus or other [flower] therein, he stirs the water in the vessel with a flower using his thumb and ring finger while uttering "Aiṃ," and then discards that flower while uttering "Klīm."

Having cast a flower moistened with the eight-fold fragrance consisting of sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, *coraka*, saffron, *rocanā*, *jaṭāmāṃsī*, and resinous extract (*śilārasa*), or else moistened with sandalwood paste and the like,
one should gaze upon it with the *gālinī* mudrā while reciting "sauḥ," and [recite] the third peak-syllable "oṃ somamaṇḍalāya."
"Obeisance to the nectar of the special *arghya* of the Śrī Paradevatā, whose self consists of the sixteen digits (*kalā*) that bestow all desires.

Having thus worshipped within the water contained in the vessel and visualized therein the previously mentioned mandala, one should worship it as before up to the five jewels (*pañcaratna*). If one is endowed with the *śāmbhavī-dīkṣā*, one should likewise [worship] with the five *praṇavas*.

One should worship as follows: Then, having invoked the sixteen digits (*kalā*) of Soma there as before (p. 175), and having performed the consecration of their vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) for them preceded by their respective names as before, one should worship them in a circular form, proceeding clockwise starting from one's own front. It is as follows: 4 *aṃ* homage to Amṛtā; 4 *āṃ*... [and so on].
Mānadāyai 4, Iṃ Pūṣāyai 4, Īṃ Tuṣṭyai 4, Uṃ Puṣṭyai 4, Ūṃ Ratyai 4,
Ṛṃ Dhṛtyai 4, Ṝṃ Śaśinyai 4, Ḷṃ Candrikāyai 4, Ḹṃ Kāntyai 4, Eṃ Jyotsnāyai 4,
Aiṃ Śrīyai 4, Oṃ Prītyai 4, Auṃ Aṅgadāyai 4, Aṃ Pūrṇāyai 4, Aḥ.

Having worshipped with "To Pūrṇāmṛtā," one should visualize a triangle within the center of the worshipped maṇḍala, consisting of three lines beginning with 'A' (the *akathādi* triangle). Within its three corners, one should contemplate the three syllables (*kūṭas*) of the root-vidyā; in the central bindu, the *kāmakalā*; on its two sides, the letters *Ha* and *Kṣa* with their respective bindus; behind them, the letter *La*; and on its two sides [the letters *Ra* and *Va*].
Having visualized the *haṃsa* syllable and formed the *yonimudrā* filled with flowers and unbroken rice grains,
one should raise the *kuṇḍalinī* from the *mūlādhāra* according to the method taught by the guru, piercing the six *cakras* in sequence along the path of the *suṣumnā*.

"O you who bring forth the nectar of immortality! You who are the great vessel filled and overflowing with the entirety of the essence produced from the lunar orb of consciousness situated in the *brahmarandhra*—bring forth the nectar of immortality! *Aiṃ plūṃ glauṃ jūṃ saḥ, amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛteśvari amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtaṃ srāvaya srāvaya svāhā!*"—thus [one recites] over that nectar of the *arghya*.

Having joined that stream of nectar by scattering flowers and unbroken rice grains, and having displayed the *dhenumudrā* while uttering "Vam," one should consecrate [the water] three times with the eight-syllable mantra of the Self, *oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so'haṃ svāhā*,
and then, reciting again, worship the *śrīpādukā* of the power of the Self (*ātmaśakti*) within the water, saying: "I worship."

Having worshipped [the water] again, consecrated it three times with the *praṇava* (OM), and worshipped it with "Haṃsaḥ Ajapāśaktiśrī," one should then consecrate it three times with the *mātṛkā* [alphabet] devoid of the *bindu*. Having uttered that [mantra] once more, one should worship it within the water with "Mātṛkāsarasvatīśrī" and then consecrate it ten times with the third *kūṭa* of the root mantra.

Again, having uttered the third peak-syllable (*kūṭa*), and having worshipped [it] in the midst of the water with "Tripurāmṛteśvarī-śrī," and having consecrated [the water] three times with the two mantras of the couple Ānandabhairava and [Ānandabhairavī], namely:
*4 hasakṣamalavarayūṃ sahakṣamalavarayīṃ*,
and *4 hasakṣamalavarayūṃ*.

"Vauṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava; I worship the *śrīpāduka* of Ānandabhairava, I satiate him, obeisance"—having thus worshipped and satiated [him] three times, [recite] "4 *sahakṣamalavarayīṃ*, *vaṣaṭ* to Sudhādevī; I worship the *śrīpāduka* of Sudhādevī"—having thus worshipped and satiated [her], [recite] "*hasauṃ*, obeisance to Varuṇa; *shauṃ*."
Having consecrated [the water] three times with the mantra "vāruṇodevyai namaḥ" by means of Varuṇa and the Varuṇa-mithuna-vidyā,

and having again recited them separately, worshipping and satiating [them] with "varuṇaśrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi tarpayāmi" and "vāruṇīdevīśrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi tarpayāmi," one should then consecrate it once each with the Bālā-mantra and the sixteen Nityā-mantras to be described hereafter.
Having consecrated [the offering] three times separately with the daily *nityā-vidyā* of that day and the *nityā-vidyā* of each respective lunar date (*tithi*),
and if one is initiated into the *ūrdhvāmnāya*, having consecrated it three times with the two mantras *hasauḥ* and *shauḥ* using the *Prāsāda*, *Parāparā*, and *Prasāda* mantras;
Then, if he has been initiated into the Caraṇa [tradition], he should consecrate [the disciple] three times with the *vidyās* of the Caraṇa-kula-yoginīs;
if he has been initiated by the *anuttara-parā-vidyā*, "sauḥ," he should consecrate him three times with that;
and if he was previously initiated, he should consecrate him three times with the *kāmakalā-vidyā*.

If [the recipient] is endowed with the Śāmbhava initiation belonging to the six lineages, then, having consecrated [the water] three times with those vidyās and then three times with the pāñcabhautika mantras to be described hereafter, one should invoke the ten kalās beginning with Sṛṣṭi into the midst of the water and perform their prāṇapratiṣṭhā as before, preceded by their respective names.

Having performed [the rite] with this verse: "Oṃ, the Haṃsa seated in purity, the Vasu seated in the intermediate space, the Hotṛ seated at the altar, the guest seated in the house; seated among men, seated in the best [place], seated in the assembly, seated in the sky; born of the waters, born of the cows, born of Truth, born of the mountains—the Great Truth. Thus, by means of this Ṛc, Vāmadeva is the Seer, Jagatī is the Metre, and Sūrya is the Deity.
Having consecrated [the water] once and recited "Oṃ Brahmaṇe Namaḥ," one should worship it in the midst of the water. Then,

having worshipped the *kalās* of the *ka*- and *ca*-groups according to the method previously described in the *Kalāmātṛkā-nyāsa*, namely "Oṃ Kaṃ Sṛṣṭyai Namaḥ" and so forth, one should thereafter invoke the ten *kalās* beginning with Old Age (*jarā*) arising from the *ṭa*- and *ta*-groups, and [worship] them as before.

Having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (invocation of the vital breaths), one should consecrate [the image] once with this verse: "Oṃ, by his heroic power Viṣṇu is praised; like a terrifying beast that wanders and dwells in the mountains, in whose three wide strides all worlds abide. Having recited this again, one should worship with "Salutation to Viṣṇu" (*viṣṇave namaḥ*) and [offer] *ṭaṃ*.

Having worshipped them with "Obeisance to Jarā" and so forth, one should again invoke the *kalās* arising from the *pa* group, beginning with Tīkṣṇā, as before; having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* for them, [one recites] "Tryambakaṃ yajāmahe"—of which Vasiṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chanda*), and Tryambaka Rudra is the deity (*devatā*). Oṃ tryambakaṃ yajāmahe.
Fragrant, the increaser of nourishment—may I be released from death as from a cucumber from its stem, yet not be released from immortality.

Having thus consecrated [the weapon] and recited [the mantra] again, one should worship with "Obeisance to Rudra" (rudrāya namaḥ), and then worship with "Obeisance to Tīkṣṇā" (tīkṣṇāyai namaḥ) and so forth. Then, having invoked the five kalās— yellow and the others— residing in the five syllables beginning with *sa* and ending with *kṣa*, one should perform the installation of their vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) for them as before.

Having consecrated [the vessel] with the Gāyatrī mantra and recited it again, one should worship it with "Oṃ, obeisance to Īśvara. Then, having worshipped those [lines] starting with "Oṃ, obeisance to Pātālā," one should subsequently invoke the Kalās, such as Nivṛtti and the rest, which arise from the vowels, and perform the Prāṇapratiṣṭhā for them as before. Then, regarding the mantra "Viṣṇu shall prepare the womb... [one should proceed].

Tvaṣṭṛ is the seer who forms the embryo; Anuṣṭubh is the meter; Śrī Viṣṇu is the deity; the application is for the sake of pleasing Sadāśiva. Having consecrated [the offering] with the mantra: "May Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms;
may Prajāpati pour [the seed]; may Dhātṛ place the embryo within you," and having recited it again for Sadāśiva...

Having worshipped with "Namaḥ" in the midst of the water, and having worshipped with "Aṃ Nivṛttyai Namaḥ" and so forth, one should consecrate [the water] twice with the Mātṛkā, recite it again, and worship with "Mātṛkāsarasvatīśrī. Then: "4 Aiṃ! O You who produce the bliss of the undivided single essence, O You who consist of supreme nectar, [grant] the spontaneous manifestation here..."
O you who possess the form of Kula, bestow [your grace].

Having consecrated [the object] three times with this [mantra], and having further consecrated it three times with: *klīṃ*, O you who abide in the *akula*, whose form is nectar, who bestows the knowledge of accomplishment, O Supreme One, bestow the state of immortality upon this substance which has a moist form; and having said: *sauḥ*, O you whose nature is this, having granted identity with my own form, become supreme nectar within me.

"Make the vibration of consciousness (citsphuraṇaṃ kuru). Having thus consecrated [the vessel] three times, and having consecrated it four times with the Amṛteśvarī-vidyā—namely: *aiṃ plūṃ hrauṃ jūṃ saḥ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛteśvari amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtaṃ srāvaya srāvaya svāhā*—and having again uttered that [mantra], [one invokes] Amṛteśvarī-Śrī.

Having thus worshipped once, one should then consecrate [the object] five times with the Dīpinī-vidyā: *aiṃ vadavada vāgvādini aiṃ klīṃ klīnnekledini kledaya kledaya mahākṣobhaṃ kuru kuru klīṃsauḥ mokṣaṃ kuru kuru sauḥ hsauḥ*. Then, having recited the root-vidyā there eight times:
Having visualized a square with a western door in the center of that [mandala],
one should worship Kula-vaṭukanātha and his consort Ambā Śrī on the right and left sides of that door respectively; then,
inside that, having worshipped the six seats as before, [one worships] in the middle of the bindu situated within the triangle in its center.

In the *Kāmakalā*, having invoked and meditated upon the Goddess according to the method to be described, and having performed the ritual integration (*sakalīkaraṇa*) through the application of the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*), one should worship her with perfumes and other offerings. Then, according to the procedure to be described, one should worship the limbs of dissolution (*layāṅga*) upon the body of the Goddess, as well as the Tithinityā, the sixteen Nityās, and the three lineages of Gurus.

Having worshipped the six-limbed *Ṣaḍaṅga-yuvatī* and offered three or one handful of flowers with the *samaṣṭi-yoginī-mantra* to be described hereafter, and having presented incense and lamps, [one offers worship] to the *yoni*, *dhenu*, *mahāyoni*, *triśikhā*, *padmasaṃkṣobha*, *drāvaṇa*, *ākarṣa*, *vaśya*, *unmāda*, *mahāṅkuśa*, *akhacarī*, *bīja*, and *yoni*.
Having displayed the eighteen mudrās known as the noose, the goad, the bow, and the arrow, one should prostrate with the *namaskāra* mudrā.
If one is unable to perform all of this here, one should perform either the consecration (*abhimantraṇa*) or the worship (*pūjana*).

If one is unable even for this, then having performed the worship ending with the eight-syllable mantra of the Self, and having fully worshipped and gratified the couple Ananda-Bhairava and Bhairavī, one should begin the worship of the Kalās starting with Sṛṣṭi and so forth, and complete the remainder as before;
such is the procedure for the installation of the special *arghya*. Then, following that, by that same procedure, the vessel called the *śrīpātra*—
One should set aside another vessel. With that [vessel], one should satisfy the deities of the surrounding enclosures (āvaraṇadevatā) other than the Root Goddess (mūladevī).
The offering of worship and so forth, as well as the libation for the Root Goddess, should be performed with the special arghya alone.
In that regard, the offering of worship and the giving of arghya for the three enclosures, beginning from Anaṅgakusumā up to the end, [are performed with it].
One should perform [the rite] with the ordinary arghya water alone—this is the procedure for the installation of the Śrīpātra.

Then, in that same sequence, one should fill two vessels below that in the form of a row for the sake of the *pādya*, *ācamanīya*, and *madhuparka* with pure water, and fill a third with the *madhuparka* ingredients; having placed a small amount of the special *arghya* water into each of them.

One should consecrate [the ingredients] individually eight times with the root mantra (*mūlavidyā*). For the honey-mixture (*madhuparka*), a bell-metal vessel (*kāṃsyapātra*) is recommended; otherwise, one should prepare it in another vessel, excluding copper vessels, and cover it with a lid.
For the general water offering (*sāmānyārghya*), there should be fragrance, flowers, unbroken rice (*akṣata*), barley, tips of *kuśa* grass, sesame seeds, mustard seeds, and *dūrvā* grass.

One should pour [the water] out. Into the vessel for the feet (pādyapātra), one should pour the eight substances known as śyāmāka rice, dūrvā grass, lotus, aparājitā flower, uśīra, and rocanā. Into the vessel for sipping water (ācamanīyapātra), one should pour the powders of nutmeg, clove, and kakkola.

In the absence of the aforementioned substances, one should pour in rice while meditating upon each respective substance. Having poured curd, honey, and clarified butter into the vessel for the *madhuparka*, one should consecrate it with a drop from the special *arghya*.

In the event that curd and the other items are unavailable, one should fill the vessel with water alone while maintaining the mental visualization of those substances. Then, to the southeast of oneself...
Having established the vessels for the water for the feet (*pādya*) and so forth according to the prescribed rule, one should likewise place the vessel for the water for sipping (*ācamanīya*).
If there is an inability to do so here as well, one may offer the triad beginning with the water for the feet in a single vessel.
Then, having learned the rules for their application from the mouth of one's own guru, one should [prepare] the four vessels according to the procedure for the general *arghya*.

One should place them beyond the *prokṣaṇī* vessel. Their names are: the Guru-vessel, the Śakti-vessel, the Vaṭuka-vessel, and the Ātman-vessel. One should consecrate the Guru-vessel with the *guru-pādukā-vidyā*, the Śakti-vessel with the *bālā-vidyā*, the Vaṭuka-vessel with its own mantra, and the Ātman-vessel with the eight-syllabled *ātman-mantra*.

One should consecrate each respective vessel eight times with its corresponding mantra. Then, with water from the *prokṣaṇī* vessel taken up in another vessel, one should recite: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ*, uttering the first *kūṭa*, and say:
*ātmatattvātmane namaḥ*. [4] *klīṃ*, uttering the second [kūṭa], and say: *vidyātattvātmane namaḥ*. [4] *sauḥ*.

Third: *śivatattvātmane namaḥ*. 4. Having recited the entire root mantra (*aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*) and saying *sarvatattvātmane namaḥ*, one sprinkles oneself; then, again with the root mantra, one sprinkles the sacrificial ground, the sacrificial implements, and the *śrīcakra*. [One should then display] the *dhenumudrā* over all objects.

"One should display [it]": this is the procedure for placing the vessels for the *arghya* and other offerings. Here, if one is unable to place the *śrīpātra*, one should perform the aforementioned worship and so forth using only the *viśeṣārghya*.

Now, the procedure for arranging the vessels in brief: there, having drawn on one's left side a mandala consisting of a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square using sandalwood paste and other substances, and having worshipped therein the fourfold pedestal, [one worships] with "4 maṃ, to the self of the ten kalās that bestow dharma."

Having worshipped with "Obeisance to the fire-mandala, the support of the pitcher of the venerable Supreme Deity," and having worshipped the ten kalās beginning with Dhūmrārcis upon it, proceeding clockwise from the east as before, one should place the pitcher— which has been washed with the Astra-mantra and well-perfumed— with "AṂ. (4)

Having worshipped with the mantra: "Obeisance to the solar disc consisting of twelve digits (kalās) that bestows wealth, which serves as the vessel for the jar of the Śrī Parādevatā," one should worship the twelve digits beginning with Tapinī in clockwise order starting from the east upon the jar; therein, [one should perform] what is prescribed according to the distinction of the qualified practitioner.
Having filled separate vessels with milk, clarified butter, honey, and any one of the fermented liquors, along with the previously consecrated substance,
while reciting the Mātṛkā in reverse and forward order together with the Root-Vidyā;
and having worshipped therein the Six-Limbed Youthful Goddesses, the three lineages of Gurus, the sixteen Nityās, the daily Nityā of that day, and Ratneśvarī.

4. Having worshipped with "Oṃ, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala, the self of the sixteen digits that bestows desires, the nectar of the jar of the Śrī Paradevatā," and having worshipped the sixteen digits beginning with Amṛtā in clockwise order starting from the east, [one should take] that nectar.

Having meditated upon [the deity] as consisting of the Supreme Brahman, one should cover it with a vessel provided with a lid and an *uddharaṇī*, and then completely cover it with a fine cloth; such is the procedure for the installation of the jar (*kalaśa*). Other vessels should also be installed according to this stated method with their respective mantras; this is the summary.

Thus [ends] the *Śrīvidyārṇava*, a Tantra composed by the ascetic Śrī Vidyāraṇya, who was a disciple of Śrī Pragalbhācārya, who was a disciple of Śrī Viṣṇuśarmācārya, who was a disciple of Śrī Bhagavat Śaṅkarācārya, who was a disciple of the venerable Śrī Govindācārya, the illustrious Great Mahopādhyāya and worshipful teacher.
The Ninth Chapter on Exhalation. 9.
Now begins the tenth breath (chapter) of the Śrīvidyārṇava Tantra.
Now, the self-worship (*ātmapūjā*): there, having placed a vessel with its base upon a triangular mandala in front of oneself,

having filled it with water from the ritual jar (*kalaśa*), and having offered a drop of the special *arghya*, one adorns one’s own body with sandalwood paste and other substances, while meditating on oneself in the form of the chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*).
Having prostrated before the Guru, Gaṇapati, and the Supreme Deity, and having meditated upon Kuṇḍalinī as before, from the *mūlādhāra* up to the *brahmarandhra*,
one should contemplate the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*) as being of that same form. Then,
visualizing one's own body as the form of one's chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*) transformed by its splendor, one should perform the self-worship (*ātmapūjā*).

Having visualized one's own body as the *yogapīṭha* according to the previously mentioned method of the *yogapīṭha-nyāsa*, and having visualized the venerable Supreme Deity seated upon the *śrīcakra* within the pericarp of the heart-lotus,
one should worship Her with the sixteen offerings (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) in the sequence to be described, [offering] five handfuls of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) upon one's own body.

Having offered incense and lamps, one should perform the internal oblation (*antarhavana*). Therein, having visualized a triangular sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) at the *mūlādhāra*, one should contemplate within its center the Fire of Time (*kālāgni*) or the Fire of Desire (*kāmāgni*),
kindled by the fuel of latent impressions (*vāsanā*) and fanned by the five vital airs beginning with *prāṇa*.

Having meditated upon the circle of the fire of consciousness presided over by the Supreme Goddess in the form of Kuṇḍalinī, one should offer the functions of the senses perpetually through the path of the Suṣumṇā, using the mind as a ladle into the fire of the Self, which blazes with the oblation of merit and demerit, preceded by the Praṇava and the three Tārās and ending with the root-mantra: "I offer this; Svāhā! Thus: *idaṃ juhomi svāhā*.

Having offered seven oblations seven times— consisting of the seven sacrificial offerings (havir-saptaka) characterized by the mental constructs and conceptualizations of merit and demerit, as well as what ought and ought not to be done— one should then grasp the Unmanī-ladle with the hands of Light (prakāśa) and Contemplation (amarśa), [and pour] the oil of the portions of dharma and adharma into the fire at the end of the root-vidyā preceded by the Praṇava and the three Tārās.

"I offer [this] into the full fire. Having offered the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the words "I offer unrighteousness, svāhā," the practitioner should remain for a few moments in the form of the partless Brahman, with the entire phenomenal world (*prapañca*) cast away. Then, having meditated upon himself in the form of the Goddess and having prostrated before the sandals of the venerable Guru (*śrīgurupādukā*), [he should proceed].
Having visualized a vessel filled with food upon one's head, having recited that mantra as many times as possible and offered it,

and having performed breath control (prāṇāyāma), the ritual syllables (ṛṣyādi), and the six-limbed placement (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa), one should recite the root mantra one hundred and eight times, offer the recitation, and offer praise.
"One should prostrate"—this refers to self-worship. Now follows the purification of the Śakti. As it is stated in the Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi:
"From association with those of the Kula who are uninitiated, the loss of accomplishment arises;
therefore, one should perform the consecration either by force or through diligent effort. (1)
First, having uttered the Bālā mantra, one should utter "to Tripurā";
having uttered the word "namaḥ," one should then speak this Śakti mantra. (2)
"Make me pure," at the end of the word [say], "make my power [pure], O Beloved";
having uttered the wife of Vahni (Svāhā), this is the purification mantra, O Sovereign of the Gods. (3)

One should utter the seed-syllable of Māyā into her ear with the thought that it is indivisible [from her]. Thus is the purification of the Śakti. Then, one should place the purified substance into the *arghya* vessel. Likewise, in the sequence of the Śrīcakra, one should deposit the previously purified substance in secret. Thus, in the *Svatantra*:

Having placed the materials for the *arghya* offering into the *arghya* vessel, the wise and self-restrained practitioner [should offer] the substance produced from the *kuṇḍa* and *goḷa*, as well as the *svayaṃbhū* flower. (1)
O Maheśānī, by offering the *arghya* one becomes a master of all supernatural powers (*siddhis*);
and through the offering of *arghya* with nectar (*sudhā*), one becomes dear to the *yoginīs*. (2)
"O Goddess, one becomes a great yogi by means of the water used for washing the sacred seats (pīṭha).
Thus it is said in the Bhairava Tantra: "There is nothing superior to the fifth [element] for Śākta practitioners seeking both worldly enjoyment and liberation."
Or even by means of the five alone, the practitioner becomes perfected.
Thus it is said:
"Then one should worship Maṇḍūka in the center of the paryaṅka, as well as Kālāgnirudra, Ādhāraśakti, Kūrma, and Ananta. (1)
One should worship Varāha as the bulbous root of the earth, with the stalk, the filaments, the lotus, the pericarp, and the mandala. || 2 ||
One should worship Dharma, dispassion, sovereignty, knowledge, as well as ignorance, lack of sovereignty, lack of dispassion, and even non-dharma. (3)
In this manner, one should also worship that which consists of knowledge and wisdom (jñāna-vidyā), as well as the Self (ātman).
Having offered perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice grains, and other such items, one should place them there. || 4 ||
Having established the lineage there above and performed the ritual worship,
one should then, with a concentrated mind, worship the five desires within that [vessel].
Having worshipped with flowers joined with perfumes, beginning with the syllable *oṃ* and ending with *namaḥ*, one should honor the Lord of the Family in the four directions.
Having first given the Vāgbhava, the Kāmarāja, and the Strībīja which is the Kāmarāja,
and then the essence of Blūṃ, one should extract the Ādhāraśakti.
"Having drawn a triangle there with vermilion and other substances, O fair-faced one," as stated in the *Uttara-tantra*:
"And having inscribed the mantra upon a triangle on her head, the practitioner..."
Then, one should worship the Great Preta-seat in the center and Bālā.
One should worship with the mantra: *hsauṃ sadāśivamahāpretapadmāsanāya namaḥ*. In the *Kulārṇava*:
"O Dear One, having worshipped Gaṇeśa, Kulādhyakṣa, Durgā, Lakṣmī, and Sarasvatī in the [outer] triangles, one should then worship Vasanta and Madana."
"Afterwards, one should worship the Moon (Sudhākara) upon her breasts and on her face.
Thus it is said. In the *Uttaratantro*:
"One should worship Gaṇeśa on the crown of the head, Kulādhyakṣa at the tips of the hair, and [the deity] on the forehead."
Likewise, one should place Durgā on the eyebrows, Lakṣmī on the tongue, and Sarasvatī [on the palate]. || 1 ||
Thus, in the Jñānārṇava:
"O beautiful one, one should worship all the digits (kalās) of both Kāma and Soma, beginning from the right foot up to the head, and from the left head down to the foot. (1)
"Faith, joy, and likewise delight," and so forth, should be seen in the *Mātṛkāśvāsa*.
As it says in the *Uttaratantro*: "In this way, one should worship with the vowels for the sake of accomplishing all tasks. And in the *Lalitātantra*:
"In her vulva, three flowing channels are to be known."
One day belongs to the Moon, while another day belongs to the Sun.
The Āgneyī and the other [Vāruṇī] are to be known; the practitioner should worship them.
The Cāndrī drips water, and the Bhānavī drips flowers.
The seed-syllable flows forth, and one should worship the fiery [deities] among them by their names;
with a well-pleased mind, one should perform the worship using [mantras] beginning with the "Vāgbhava" syllable and joined with "namaḥ. || 3 ||
Thus it is said in the *Uttaratantra*:
"One should worship in the temple of Madana, which is smeared with red sandalwood;
having first uttered the *Bhagamālā-mantra*, and likewise after the *Tritārā*. (1)
Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ jūṃ blūṃ, and likewise klinne, and after that [sarvāṇi] bhagāni, [then] vaśamānaya me. || 2 ||
"Strīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ blūṃ, obeisance to Bhagamālinī.
With this mantra—*aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*—one should worship her with perfumes and other offerings.
O Maheśvarī, here too there is no invocation (*āvāhana*), nor the ritual placement of the vital breaths (*jīvanyāsa*).
Then, having worshipped the chosen deity according to this procedure with the sixteen types of offerings, one shall become a master of all supernatural attainments.
Immediately thereafter, one should worship one's own Śiva with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings;
then [one should recite] the root mantra, namely "Oṃ namo śivāya. (5)
One should worship with those known as Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Sadyojāta, and so forth; and immediately thereafter, one should [worship] Tāra (Oṃ) and Śāntyatītā upon their limbs.
"Having recited the complete vidyā, one should worship the triangle.
Thus it is said in the Uttaratantra: "One should also worship Avadhūteśvarī, Kubjā, Kāmākhyā, and Samayā."
Vajreśvarī, Kālikā, and likewise Dikcaravāsinī.
There the practitioner should worship Mahācaṇḍeśvarī Tārā;
then, having offered betel-leaf and obtained her permission, [he should proceed].
And having cast Śiva there with the mudrā called Gajatuṇḍa,
[one should offer him] into the fire of the self, which is kindled by the oblation of dharma and adharma, using the mind as a sacrificial ladle.
"By means of the path of Suṣumṇā, I constantly offer the functions of the senses;
svāhā—this great mantra, ending with 'svāhā', is proclaimed for the commencement. (4)
Then, while approaching a woman, one should recite the Vidyā Trirbhuvaneśvarī three times,
supported by the hands of Prakāśa and Ākāśa with the ladle of Unmanī.
(180) "I offer into the fire that which is filled with the essence of merit and demerit and the oil of attachment;
svāhā. This great mantra, ending in *svāhā*, is proclaimed for the relinquishing of semen. || 6 ||
Thus, in the Jñānārṇava: "The union of Śiva and Śakti is indeed yoga, without a doubt; the sound 'sīt' is the form of the mantra, and speech becomes praise. (1)
Embracing is musk and camphor;
kissing becomes [the offering of] various flowers such as nail-marks, tooth-marks, and the like. (2)
"Know that sexual union (*maithuna*) is satisfaction (*tarpaṇa*), and the emission of semen (*vīryapāta*) is its release (*visarjana*).
Thus it is said in the *Kulārṇava*:
"Embracing, kissing, and likewise the massaging of the breasts..."
The sight and touch of the vulva, as well as the rubbing of the male organ against it, constitute [the offense]. || 1 ||
"One should worship the nine flowers with the entry and the stabilization of the power.
Thus it is said in the *Yāmala*:
"From union arises bliss characterized by supreme bliss."
A man should diligently take up the nectar of the lineage, for it is difficult to obtain. || 1 ||
Indeed, by that divine nectar, all become satisfied;
whatever desire the mantra-practitioner undertakes, that is accomplished in an instant. || 2 ||
Thus, in the Jñānārṇava:

"O Dear One, having purified the substance of the Kula, which consists of Śiva and Śakti, O Beautiful One, one should cast it [into the vessel] while reciting the seed-syllable nectar, the Supreme Brahman. (1)

By diligently honoring the sequence of Śrīvidyā with the nectar from the arghya vessel, one who is always free from fault and devoid of conceptual construction shall become identical with the Supreme Brahman. || 2 ||
Thus has this knowledge, the essence and the beautiful, been told to you, O fair-faced one;
for a man who is constantly possessed of conceptual construction becomes a partaker of sin. (3)
A practitioner who is dominated by doubt becomes one who violates the Guru’s bed;
therefore, O lady of beautiful hips, he should always remain free from conceptual construction.
Thus, in the Kulārṇava:
"The wise one, having taken the *kulāmṛta*, should place it into that *arghya*;
having worshipped with that *arghya*, he should complete the remainder of the worship. (1)
The purified [substance] is designated as *kulāmṛta* (the nectar of the clan). The purification mantra, however, is found in the *Śrīkrama*:
Oṃ, O Amṛtā, born of nectar, showerer of nectar, beloved!
O Goddess, release the two words "pada" from the curse of Śukra. (1)
Causing the pair to flow as nectar, make the two-fold yoga into nectar;
then, O Goddess, by the word *svāhā*, O Beloved, the purification of the semen occurs.
O Goddess of the Gods, one should worship the Goddess in the *yoni* with white unbroken rice grains, fragrant flowers, and substances for the *arghya* offering.

Thus, in the *Uttaratantra*: "The practitioner of the Kula, having performed worship with incenses, lamps, and various food offerings, and having prostrated to her, should himself consume her remains. (1)
Thus it is said; and in the Śivāgama:
"If one drinks the *śaktyucchiṣṭa* without discernment in the presence of the *cakra*, he goes to a terrible hell and certainly falls from the Kula path. (1)
Therefore, having reflected with effort, the wise one should drink the remnant of the power;
the hero should bring about bliss and drink that reality free from delusion. (2)

Thus, the purification of power (*śakti-śodhana*) has been explained in brief; the specific details, however, will be stated later in the ritual procedure (*prayoga-vidhi*). Now, regarding the ritual for the worship of the throne (*pīṭha-pūjā*): having sprinkled the *śrīcakra* with the water of the offering (*arghya*), one should recite the mantra of the Guru’s sandals (*gurupādukā-vidyā*) over the throne to one's left, [beginning with] "The venerable sandals of [Name] Ānandanātha."
