Ūṃ Manoramā-pādaḥ | 2 | Ṛṃ Manoharā-pādaḥ | 2 | Ṝṃ Manorathā-pādaḥ | 2 | Ḷṃ Madanā-pādaḥ | 2 | Ḹṃ Unmādinī-pādaḥ | 2 | Eṃ Mohinī-pādaḥ | 2 | Aiṃ Śaṅkhinī-pādaḥ | 2 | Oṃ Śoṣiṇī-pādaḥ | 2 | Auṃ Vaśaṃkarī-pādaḥ | 2 |
Having worshipped with "2 Aṃ Śiñjinīpādukāṃ" and "2 Aḥ Subhagāpādukāṃ," then outside of that,
at the tips of the sixteen petals: "2 Aṃ Pūṣāpādukāṃ," "2 Āṃ Idhāpādukāṃ," "2 Iṃ Sumanasāpādukāṃ," "2 Iṃ Ratipādukāṃ," "2 Uṃ Prītipādukāṃ," "2 Ūṃ Dhṛtipādukāṃ."
Ṛṃ—Ṛddhipāda; 2 Ṝ—Saumyāpāda; 2 Ḷ—Marīcipāda; 2 Ḹṃ—Aṃśumālinīpāda;
2 Eṃ—Śaśinīpāda; 2 Aiṃ—Aṅgirāpāda; 2 Oṃ—Chāyāpāda; 2 Auṃ—Saṃpūrṇamaṇḍalāpāda; 2 Aṃ—Tuṣṭipāda; 2 Aḥ—Amṛtāpāda. Thus.

Having worshipped [the deity], outside of that, in the six corners—starting from the corner with its apex pointing south: 2 Aiṃ Āḍākinī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi; in the corner with its apex pointing north: 2 Aiṃ Rākiṇī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi; in the rear corner: 2 Aiṃ Lākinī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi; in the rear-left corner:
2 Aiṃ Kākinī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi; in the rear-right corner: 2 Aiṃ Śākinī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi; in front of the Goddess: 2 Aiṃ Hākinī-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi.
Having thus worshipped, one should worship within the square outside the hexagon:
in the southeast corner, *2 aiṃ vaṭukapā* [oṃ vaṭukabhairavāya pādyaṃ kalpayāmi]; in the southwest, *2 gaṃ gaṇapatipā*; in the northwest, *aiṃ durgāpā*;
and in the northeast, *2 aiṃ kṣaṃ kṣetreśapā*. Having thus worshipped, [one proceeds] outside that, in the square of the Goddess...

Beginning from the rear and proceeding through the ten directions starting with the east, one should worship the world-protectors (lokapālas) and their weapons with their respective names ending in *śakti*, as follows: "2 aiṃ laṃ, obeisance to Indra-śakti"; "2 aiṃ raṃ, obeisance to Agni-śakti," and so forth. Having performed the worship of the incense, lamp, and food offering (*naivedya*), one should then offer the *kurukullā-bali*.
Having offered the bali-oblation to Vaṭuka, Gaṇapa, Durgā, and the Kṣetreśas, one should complete the remainder of the rite, such as the recitation (*japa*) and so forth.
Here, among the fifteen *Nityās* as well, the bali for all beings (*sarvabhūtabali*) is offered at the beginning of the worship and at the conclusion of the worship.
One should offer the bali-oblation to Kurukullā with the seven-syllable mantra; this is the procedure for the worship of Kāmeśvarī Nityā.
Now follows the procedure for the worship of the eternal goddess Bhagamālinī. Regarding this, the *Śrītantrarāja* states (chapter 8):
"Now, among the sixteen eternal goddesses (*nityās*), listen, O Goddess, as I shall explain in due order the third, Bhagamālinī, together with her limbs (*aṅga*) and her enclosures (*āvaraṇa*). (1)
Then its limbs, that meditation, the deities who are its obstructions,
the sequence of its worship, and likewise the extraction of the mantra;
Kāmeśvarī and others are the beginning, then Rasa, Sthirā, and Rasā.
Subsequently, Dharāyuk is with the moving; thereafter, Sthira is known as Rasa. || 3 ||
When *sthirā* is joined with *agni* and *śūnya*, it becomes *rasa*; immediately after that, *sthirā* joined with *bhū* and *gotrā* results in *sadāha-agnī-rasa-sthirā*. (4)
Then the sky was joined with the wind, and the water was endowed with mobility;
thereafter, the water became solidified and was subsequently joined with the wind.
Ambu (water) is with Haṃsa (the letter *ha*) and Cara (the letter *ra*), and then Rasa (taste) is joined with Sthira (the letter *tha*).
Haṃsa (the letter *ha*) is conjoined with Sthira (the letter *dha*), and then with Vyāpta (the letter *ya*) and Cara (the letter *ra*). (6)
Rasa, Sthirā, then Vyāptam, Bhūyutam, Śūnyam, Agniyuk; Rasa, Sthirā, then Sāgni, Śūnyam, Javiyuta, Marut. (7)
The king [is] zero joined with fire; heart-burning follows from water [and] earth;
taste [is] stable water; and space joined with itself is indeed breath. (8)
The letter *da* is the fierce fire; therefore, the earth (*kṣmā*) is stable when conjoined with burning.
The letter *sa* is mobile and swift; one should know these from the third [letter] onwards in sequence.
Then there is a group of four vowels, followed by the sixth [vowel] (rasa), and then the stable one (sthirā) joined with the heart (hṛt) and water (ambu);
then burning (dāha) with earth (kṣmā), moving (sacara), and the swift one (javī) with the heart (hṛt). 10.
Dāha (the letter ṭha) is joined with water and wind; likewise, the sky (the letter ra) is joined with fire and taste (the letter la).
Sthirā (the letter tha), however, is joined with wind; the void (the letter ha) is joined with fire, and the two moving in the sky (the letters kha and pha).
The swan (haṃsa) is joined with the pervasive wind (marut); from that, the void (śūnya) and the pervasive water (ambu) arise;
burning (dāha) is joined with the mountain (gotrā), and likewise burning is joined with speed (raya). 12.
The heart (ha) together with the earth (la), followed by the burning (ra) and the moving (ya);
then the essence (va), the firm (stha), and then the vital breath (pra) together with the essence (va) and fire (ra). (13)
Then, first a pair of zeros joined with the letter *ca* (cha), and after that, another pair of zeros;
then *go* (ga) and *trā* (tra), joined with fire (*da*) and water (*ba*), and the letter *ca* (cha). (14)
Prāṇa is conjoined with Rasācara; beyond that, it is pervaded by Gotrā.
Gotrā is conjoined with Dāhamaru; therefore, it should be pervaded by Ambu. || 15 ||
Vāta and Nabhas are joined with Bhū; Vāyu is endowed with Cara.
Rasa is joined with Sthira, Ambu, and Agni; Vāyu is conjoined with a pair of Caras. (16)
The *grāsa* is followed by *dharā* (earth) joined with *rasa* (taste) and accompanied by *śakti*;
O Goddess, the *grāsa* is joined with *bhū* (earth), and then the *rasa* pervades the heart. (17)

By burning, O auspicious lady, there is water, then the heart, followed by the mountains accompanied by water and wind; then the void alone, and finally the taste along with all moving and stationary beings.
The sky (viyat) joined with water (ambu) is Dāha; fire (agni) joined with itself is Śuci;
earth (bhūmi) joined with taste (rasa) and earth (akṣmā) with itself is [the next]; these five are situated at intervals of one. || 19 ||

The five elements, beginning with Earth, conjoined with their own respective seeds and separated by those [seeds], are indeed [the letters]: Jya, Sacara, Rasa, Bhu, and Nabha-yuta, in their proper order. (20)
The *haṃsa* (ha-sa) should be followed by two *cara* (ra); then the *prāṇa* (a) joined with *rasa* (6) and *agni* (3);
then a pair of *śūnya* (0) joined with *cara* (ra); and *hṛd-dāha* (ha-ra) joined with *ambu* (va) and *marut* (ya). || 21 ||

Then, O Dear One, one should utter *vyoma* (ha) together with *agni* (ra), followed by *rasa* (va) made stable by *marut* (ya); then *śūnya* (kha) with *agni* (ra), and *namaḥ* (namaḥ) accompanied by *cara* (pha). (22)
After water comes space, from that [comes] the sky accompanied by wind;
and the void is pervaded by the heart, joined with its own fires of speed and heat.
The *haṃsa* (the letter *ha*) should always be joined with *sadāha* (the letter *ra*), *ambu* (the letter *ba*), *rasa* (the letter *ṣa*), and *acara* (the letter *ya*).
It is taught that the final [syllable] is the *haṃsa* joined with *dāhavahni* (the letter *ra*) and *svaira* (the letter *va*). (24)
"With thirty-five hundred syllables, this Nityā Bhagamālinī shall be [established].
Thus: Aiṃ bhagabhuge bhaginī bhagodari bhagamāle bhagāvahe bhagaguhye bhagayoni bhaganipātini sarvabhagavaśaṅkari bhagarūpe nityaklinne.

O you whose nature is the *bhaga*, bring all *bhagas* unto me; O giver of boons, O one of excellent seed, O one with moistened seed, O you who are wet with the *bhaga*, O you whose fluid is moist, make them wet, make them flow; O infallible one, O you who pierce the *bhaga*, agitate, cause all beings to tremble, O Mistress of the *bhaga*.
Aiṃ blūṃ jaṃ blūṃ bheṃ blūṃ moṃ blūṃ heṃ blūṃ heṃ klinne sarvāṇi bhagāni me vaśam ānaya strīṃ hra bleṃ hrīṃ. Thus [it is said]. In the *Tripurārṇava*:
"The seer of this [mantra] is Subhaga; Gāyatrī is declared to be its meter."
But this deity, O beloved, has as its seed-syllable the nature of the letters Ha, Ra, Ba, La, and Ma.
O Supreme Goddess, Śakti is the seed-syllable of Śrī, while the last is the kīlaka.
Thus [ends the section on] Bhagamālinī Nityā. In the *Tantrarāja* (8.3):
"The limbs [of the mantra] shall consist of its syllables; the heart is said to be formed by the first [syllable].
Then the head shall be formed by four [syllables], and the crest-lock (*śikhā*) is said to be formed by three. 1.
The remaining six limbs are, in sequence, [formed] by three groups of four;
[one should meditate on] Aruṇā, who resembles the dawn, beautiful, with a face of gentle smiles. (2)
She has three eyes, is endowed with six arms, and is seated upon a lotus; in her left hands, she holds a white water-lily, a noose, a red lotus, and a sugarcane bow.
Holding in her right hands a lotus, a goad, and a flowery arrow,
she is surrounded on all sides by her own Śaktis who are likewise endowed with these same attributes.
Through other [mantras] arising from syllables, which consist of the intoxication and madness of passion,
and through those consisting of three hundred and thirty-five syllables, there is the fivefold power (śaktipañcaka) of Rūpiṇī.
Having joined the seven-syllable mantra, one should worship as many Śaktis as there are syllables:
Madanā, Mohinī, Lolā, Bhañjanī, Udyamā, and Śubhā.
She is the refreshing, the melting, the affection, the passion, the red-colored, the mind-delighting;
she is the intoxication of all, the happiness of all, the one who possesses breaking waves, and the one who exerts herself on every side.
In the manifestation of various disturbances, these powers (śaktis) are not few and their glory is manifest;
indeed, they amount to one hundred and fifty-five.
One should worship that Goddess, surrounded by them, for the attainment of one's desires.
Now, O Goddess, listen to the sequence of worship which bestows all objectives. (9)
Having constructed two squares by which the entire universe, both moving and stationary, shall come under one's control, one should then make a door on the western side.

In the center of that, having fashioned a five-petalled lotus, one should place two yonis within its pericarp; then, by means of drawing a transverse line through the middle, [the design is completed].
The Yoni should be made in that same number; thus the Yonis are proclaimed.
Having established the Śaktis within them, one should worship them, starting from the front and proceeding in reverse order.
Having drawn two circles in the center, there [one should draw] with twenty lines.
Having produced that many wombs, one should worship Madanā and the others.
In the intervals between the [principal] rites, however, one should worship the six limbs in sequence on all sides;
in the center of that, one should invoke Bhagamālā, whose form has been described.
One should worship [the deity] with the ritual services (upacāra) joined with the rites of installation (saṃsthāpana) and so forth;
having established [the vessel] with the root mantra and sprinkled it with water, one should offer the guest-water (arghya) along with the limbs (aṅga-mantras) and the root mantra.
One should likewise worship the powers of passion and aversion on both sides of the door;
and sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as before.
Between those two ends, one should likewise worship the six limbs;
within that, in the garland of bhagas, one should likewise worship Madana and the others.
One should worship the goddess situated in the center and also her weapons;
then, one should worship the goddess with the sixteen services (upacāras) as they have been described.
One should worship with the first syllable and offer those two oblations;
one should daily recite the mantra one hundred and eight times before the Goddess.
Having performed the opening of the fire as before, one should perform the oblation (homa) in ten parts;
having joined her into the Bindu as before, one should likewise worship her with the root mantra.
O Maheśvarī, one should withdraw [the deity] into one's own self according to the stated method;
thus, with the self of the Goddess, one shall bring under control the entire world—men, women, and kings.

Thus [ends the section]. Now, the ritual application (*prayoga*): there, having performed as before everything from the worship of the seat (*āsana*) up to the placement of the *yogapīṭha*, one should perform three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*). Then, one should offer salutation: "Salutation to the sage Subhaga on the head; salutation to the Gāyatrī metre on the mouth; salutation to the eternal goddess Śrī Bhagamālinī on the heart."

Salutation to the Deity. Salutation to the seed-syllable *harableṃ* at the secret place (*guhya*). Salutation to the power (*śakti*) *śrīṃ* at the two feet. Salutation to the pin (*kīlaka*) *hrīṃ* at the navel. Having thus performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*), one should say with palms joined, "The application (*viniyoga*) is for the recitation (*japa*) for the sake of attaining my desired goal. Then: *Oṃ*, salutation to the heart; *Oṃ bhagasubhage*.

Having performed the ritual placement of the six limbs on the hands (*kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) with the mantras: "To the head, svāhā! Oṃ, Bhaginī, to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), vaṣaṭ! Oṃ, Bhagodari, to the armor (*kavaca*), hūṃ! Oṃ, Bhagamāle, to the three eyes (*netratraya*), vauṣaṭ! Oṃ, Bhagāvahe, to the weapon (*astra*), phaṭ!", and having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) with the root-mantra as before.
Having meditated upon [the goddess] Aruṇā and others in the form described above, and having performed the mental worship (*mānasapūjā*),

one should prepare on a plate of gold or other materials a square pathway measuring four finger-breadths wide, divided internally and externally by two squares using saffron and other pigments; then, of that [pathway]—
Having constructed a door in the middle of the western side, one should fashion a five-petalled lotus in the center of that square; then, within its pericarp— which is endowed with two circles—
one should draw a figure with three equal lines, whose tips form angles clearly touching the circle in the center of the pericarp, according to the prescribed measurements.
Having formed the *yoni*, one should divide one of its lines into twenty-four parts;

having made twenty-three marks with those divisions, and having done the same for the other three lines as well, one should omit a measurement equal to one part on all sides and, within that space, draw three equal lines as before.

Having fashioned a *yoni*, one should divide a single line within that *yoni* twenty-one times; having thus made twenty marks per line across all three lines, one should proceed from mark to mark in sequence through those outer and inner marks until reaching forty-five.
"One should draw horizontal lines on each side. When this is done,
there arise one hundred and thirty-five triangles, formed by the intersection of the tips of the outer lines and the tips of the inner lines.
Having produced a circle by rotation such that its lines touch the three sides of the triangle at their ends,

and having likewise constructed another circle within it by rotation with a radius equal to one-fifth of that [original] diameter, and then having made yet another circle within that with a radius equal to one part;
Having tripled the measurement of the diameter of the two previously mentioned circles— each increased by one-sixteenth of its own diameter— and having divided that total measurement into ten parts,
one should mark ten points on each of the two circles surrounding it with one part of those divisions, and then, in sequence, [proceed] upon them.
Therefore, one should draw twenty horizontal lines in the manner of a *gomūtrikā* (cow-urine pattern), extending from the interior to the exterior and from the exterior to the interior. Thus,
[page 193].

When this is done, twenty equilateral triangles with their vertices clearly touching the outer and inner perimeters arise on all sides. Having thus constructed the worship-circle (*pūjācakra*) and placed it before oneself as previously described, one should [conceive] the form by means of the *bhagamālinī* mantra.

Having performed the ritual visualization (saṃkalpa) and the offerings beginning with the invocation (āvāhana) up to the presentation of flowers, one should worship the three lineages of gurus— beginning with Prakāśa and Ānanda— as before, within the circle on the back of the Goddess;
then, in the space between the two circles situated within the pericarp of the five-petaled lotus.

As before, having worshipped the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) in the directions of Agni, Īśāna, Asura, and Vāyu, as well as in front of the Goddess and in the four cardinal directions starting from that point,
one should worship on the left and right sides of the door with: "Oṃ Aiṃ Rāgaśaktipādukāṃ pūjayāmi" and "Oṃ Aiṃ Dveṣaśaktipādukāṃ pūjayāmi."
Having worshipped the one hundred and thirty-five Śaktis in the space between the two *yoni*s situated within the pericarp of the five-petalled lotus,
[one proceeds] from the front of the Goddess in the twenty triangles located within the space between the two inner circles.
In a counter-clockwise direction: *Oṃ aiṃ madanāpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. Likewise:

*mohinīpādukāṃ* twice, *lolāpādukāṃ* twice, *bhañjinīpādukāṃ* twice, *udyamāpādukāṃ* twice, *śubhāpādukāṃ* twice, *hlādinīpādukāṃ* twice, *drāviṇīpādukāṃ* twice, *prītipādukāṃ* twice, *ratipādukāṃ* twice, *raktāpādukāṃ* twice, and *manoramāpādukāṃ* twice.

Having worshipped with "Sarvonmādāpāyaḥ svāhā," "Sarvasukhāpāyaḥ svāhā," "Abhaṅgāpāyaḥ svāhā," "Abhitodyamāpāyaḥ svāhā," "Analpāpāyaḥ svāhā," "Vyaktivibhavāpāyaḥ svāhā," "Vividhavigrahāpāyaḥ svāhā," and "Kṣobhavigrahāpāyaḥ svāhā," one should then divide the circular path within that [space] into six parts by means of lines, and [worship] in those six [sections].

In the sections, beginning from the foremost section of the Goddess, one should worship with: "Oṃ Aiṃ, obeisance to the sugarcane bow," and likewise [repeating] for the noose, the *kahlāra* lily, the lotus, the goad, and the flower-arrows; having thus worshipped, and having worshipped the circular path within that, one should offer all things such as incense, lamps, and so forth.
One should conclude as before; this is the procedure for the daily worship of Bhagamālinī Nityā.
Now follows the procedure for the daily worship of Nityaklinnā. Regarding this, the Śrītantrarāja states (Chapter 9, Verse 1):
"Now, O Pārvatī, hear concerning the fourth among the sixteen Nityās, she who is named Nityaklinnā; her mantra has been previously declared."
Thus it is said. Its extraction is given in that very same work (3.32):
"The Haṃsa, joined with the fire of burning and stability, is stated first;
it shall be the eight letters beginning with the third of Kāmeśvarī. (1)
The heart-mantra joined with the wind (ha), and the *haṃsa* joined with the wind (sa)—
this eleven-syllable mantra is proclaimed as the eternal Nityaklinnā.
Thus it is said. Likewise: "Its limbs, its meditation, its powers, and worship by means of them.
In the *Tripurārṇava*:
"Brahmā is declared to be the seer (*ṛṣi*); the *virāṭ* meter is thus proclaimed."
The deity is said to be Nityaklinnā, the supreme woman who bestows fluidity. || 1 ||

"The seed-syllable is the first; the fire-born woman (*vahnijāyā*) is the power (*śakti*); it is considered to have many *kīlakas*. Thus, in the *Tantrarāja* (9.3): "The heart is declared by means of the first syllable of the mantra."
Then again by two, by two, by two, by two, and by two. || 1 ||

One should perform the remaining ancillary rites and place them sequentially upon the two hands; wherever the six-limbed rite (*ṣaḍaṅga*) is prescribed in a tantra, it should be performed there on both hands.
One should place [the mantras] upwards, starting from the base of the thumbs and ending at the tips of the little fingers;
having placed the remainder on both palms, one places them on the heart, the two eyes, the two ears, and the two nostrils.
One should place the syllables *arṇa* on the skin, the banner, the anus, and the two feet;
[one should meditate on her] as red, resembling the color of dawn, and wearing red garments.
She wore saffron garlands and unguents, her lotus-face was beautifully smiling,
her countenance shone with three eyes, and on her forehead were pearls of perspiration from the heat of meditation.
She was resplendent, her head adorned with a crown featuring a shimmering crescent moon,
and she held in her four arms a noose, a goad, and a drinking vessel.
Having thus meditated upon the eternal Nityaklinnā, who bears fearlessness, sits upon a lotus, and is languid with passion, one should worship her along with her own Śaktis.
The powers residing in the triangle and other [geometrical figures] are Kṣobhiṇī, Mohinī, and Lolā;
they are Nityā, Nirañjanā, Klinnā, Kledinī, and Madanāturā.
Madadravā, Drāviṇī, and Draviṇā reside upon the eight petals;
then Madāvilā, Maṅgalā, Manmathārtā, and Manasvinī. || 9 ||
Moha, Āmodā, Mānamayī, Māyā, Mandā, and Manovatī—these goddesses, who move with graceful gait and possess eyes red and tremulous with passion, are to be worshipped. || 10 ||
Endowed with the forms, colors, arms, and weapons of the intermediate Nityās,
one should construct two squares provided with gates facing east and west.
In the center of that [space], there is an eight-petaled lotus, and likewise in its center, a triangle;
having performed the offering (arghya) with the root-mantra and the six limbs, he should worship her while facing the east.
In the square, one should worship her starting from the west and ending at the southwest;
one should worship those ten goddesses at the sides of the doors, in the corners, and in the cardinal directions. || 13 ||

In the interval between those, one should worship those eight Śaktis on the eight petals, starting from the west and proceeding clockwise; they are located within the corners of the yoni situated therein.

From the center, one should perform three circumambulations clockwise with the power-mantras according to the prescribed method, in the regions of the northwest, northeast, and southeast, located within the pericarp and the womb [of the lotus].

One should worship the six limbs in sequence in the directions starting from the northwest (nir-ṛti) and in front; then one should worship that goddess Nityaklinnā with the aforementioned [mantras]. (16)
One should worship with ritual services and offer the bali-oblation as before;
in front of that, one should recite the vidyā a thousand times, or perhaps a hundred.
Then, having worshipped Śivā, one should perform the fire-oblation (homa) according to the prescribed sequence,
using food sprinkled with clarified butter, or clarified butter itself, or with fragrant flowers.
One should perform the oblation in the previously mentioned number as before, and conclude it as before;
then, having worshipped the Goddess and dissolved her into one's own self as previously described.
"Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and recited the pair of hymns, one should conduct oneself as being absorbed in that.

Thus [it is said]. Now, the practical application (*prayoga*): therein, as before, after the ritual worship of the seat (*āsana-pūjā*) and so forth up to the end of the *yogapīṭha-nyāsa*, one should perform three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the *Nityaklinnā* mantra, and [place it] on the head for Brahmā, the seer (*ṛṣi*).

Salutation! Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Salutation to the Virāj metre in the mouth; salutation to the deity Śrī-Nityāklinnā-nityā in the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* in the secret place; salutation to the power (*śakti*) Svāhā in the two feet; salutation to the pin (*kīlaka*) *nn* in the navel"—[all this is done] for the sake of attaining all my desired goals.

Having said "This is the application" (*viniyogaḥ*) with palms joined in reverence, one performs the six-limbed ritual placement (*kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) as follows: *hrīṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *nitya* to the head, *svāhā*;
*klinne* to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*; *mada* to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*; *drave* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*;
and *svāhā* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. Then, one places *hrīṃ namaḥ* upon the heart.
Niṃ namaḥ to the right eye; tyaṃ namaḥ to the left; kliṃ namaḥ to the right ear; nneṃ namaḥ to the left;
maṃ namaḥ to the right nostril; daṃ namaḥ to the left; draṃ namaḥ to the skin; veṃ namaḥ to the genitals; svāṃ namaḥ to the anus; hāṃ namaḥ to the two feet.
Having performed the placement [of mantras] in this manner and having executed the pervasive [placement] with the root-vidyā as before, one should—
after the mental worship beginning with meditation— draw two squares on a plate of gold or other material using saffron and so forth, provided with two doors in the east and west.

In the center of that, having fashioned an eight-petaled lotus and having made a triangle with its apex facing oneself within its pericarp, one should place it before oneself as previously described, worship it, perform the installation of the *arghya* and other offerings, and conclude with the self-worship (*ātmapūjā*).

Having worshipped the Bhuvaneśvarī-pīṭha, one should there fashion her form by means of the Nityaklinnā-vidyā; then, after the offerings beginning with the invocation and ending with flowers, one should worship the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) surrounding the Goddess within the corners as before, and outside of that, behind the Goddess, as before.

Having worshipped the three lineages of gurus beginning with Prakāśa and Ānanda, one should worship within the square in front of the Goddess, to the right of its door: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ madāvilāpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ*; to the left: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ maṅgalāpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ*. Thus, twice.

Having worshipped [the goddesses] in a clockwise direction— namely Manmathārtā, Manasvinī, Mohā, Āmodā, Mānamayī, Māyā, Mandā, and Manovatī— beginning from the front corner of the Goddess within the inner triangles: 2...
Having worshipped [the goddesses] in clockwise order as Kṣobhiṇī-pāda, Mohinī-pāda, and Lolā-pāda, one should again worship Nityaklinnā in the center with her vidyā.
Having performed all the rites such as incense, lamps, and so forth, one should conclude as before. This is the procedure for the daily worship of the goddess Nityaklinnā.
Now, the procedure for the daily worship of Bheruṇḍā is written. Regarding this, in the *Śrītantrarāja* (Chapter 10, Verse 1):
"Now, among the sixteen Nityās, she who is the fifth is Bheruṇḍā;
O wise one, listen to her ritual procedure as I describe it according to the rule."
The extraction of the mantra occurred in the third [chapter], as did the limbs, the deities of the enclosures,
and the sequence of worship.
As for the extraction of the mantra, it is stated in the third chapter (3.35):
First, *bhūḥ* is joined with its own [seed-syllable]; then *prāṇa* is joined with that by means of burning;
then *rasa* is joined with that by means of burning; and finally *prāṇa* is joined with the *vanaspati*. || 1 ||
The syllable *kaṃ* joined with *dāha*, the radiance (*prabhā*) joined with *dāha*, and the bowstring (*jyā*) joined with *dāha*; finally, the two [syllables] *nityaklinna*. (2)
"This nine-syllabled Nityā Bheruṇḍā bestows all accomplishments.
Thus: Oṃ kroṃ bhroṃ kroṃ jhroṃ chroṃ jroṃ svāhā. In the Tripurārṇava:
"The seer of this [mantra] is Mahāviṣṇu; Gāyatrī is said to be the meter."
O lady of excellent hips, this deity is said to be the third seed-syllable. || 1 ||
"The wife of Vahni (the letter *ra*) shall be the Śakti, and the goad (the letter *sa*) shall indeed be the Kīlaka.
Thus it is said. In the Tantrarāja (10.4):
"One should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅgaka*) with the six [syllables] situated at the beginning, the end, and the two [sides] of the middle."
In the apertures, the face, the mouth, the throat, the heart, the navel, and the two bases.
One should place the nine syllables of the mantra preceded by the placement of the Mātṛkās;
thereafter, O Pārvatī, listen to the meditation on the Śaktis residing within their sheaths.
On the outer enclosure, however, one should worship Brāhmī and the others, as well as the powers of the Yugas;
within that, on the eight petals, [one should worship] Vijayā, Vimalā, and Śubhā.
One should [worship] Viśvā, Vibhūti, Vinatā, and the various Vimalā in sequence; in the intermediate octagonal corners, likewise Kamalā and Kāminī.
One should worship Kirātī, Kīrtisahitā, Kurdinī, Kulasundarī,
Kalyāṇī, and Kākakolā according to the prescribed yoga.
One should worship Ḍākinī, Rākiṇī, likewise Lākinī, Kākinī, Śākinī, and Hākinī, in the six corners in successive order.
One should worship the powers of will, knowledge, and action in the three corners;
one should worship the eight weapons in the intermediate spaces of the eight corners.
Having constructed two squares provided with four gates,
one should then place an eight-petaled lotus between them, followed by a pair of circles in the interior.
From two pairs of ground squares, one should form an eight-sided figure provided with a circle;
within that, one should likewise construct a hexagonal form.
Within that [triangle], one should fashion such a womb (yoni); in its center, one should worship Bheruṇḍā, the fifth eternal goddess, surrounded by the aforementioned Śaktis.
Having prepared the *arghya* with the two root-mantras of the six limbs, one should worship facing the east;
and one should offer the *bali* oblation with the sixteen-syllable mantra at the beginning and the end in due order.
Now I shall explain the meditation that accomplishes all goals for the Goddess;
O Pārvatī, listen to the sequence of the powers residing within its rotations. 12.
Her body resembled molten gold, she was endowed with three eyes,
her face was graced with a beautiful smile, and she was adorned with divine ornaments.
Adorned with earrings, necklaces, armlets, and clusters of jewels,
she was exceedingly beautiful with ornaments such as anklets and waves of nectar.
Holding a noose and a goad, a shield and a sword, and always a vajra, a bow, and arrows with her hands— seated during worship, or otherwise standing.
And one should likewise worship the Śaktis on all sides, who possess forms identical to His and are endowed with splendor and weapons, their faces always serene with smiles. 16.
In this manner, one should worship the Goddess surrounded by her enclosures;
likewise, one should offer the bali-oblation at the beginning and the end, according to the procedure previously described.

Thus. Now, the ritual application (*prayoga*): therein, as before, having performed the worship of the seat (*āsana-pūjā*) and so forth, up to the end of the placement on the *yogapīṭha*, one should perform three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the *bheruṇḍā-vidyā*. Then, on the head: *oṃ mahāviṣṇave ṛṣaye namaḥ*; in the mouth: *gāyatrīcchandase namaḥ*; in the heart—
Salutation to the deity Śrī Bheruṇḍānityā. Salutation to the seed-syllable *Bhrāṃ* at the secret place (*guhya*).

Salutation to the power (*śakti*) *Svāhā* at the two feet. Salutation to the *kīlaka* *Kroṃ* at the navel. Having thus performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), one should say with palms joined, "This is the application for the attainment of all my desired goals," and then [recite] *Kroṃ* to the heart.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs upon the hands with: *namaḥ*; *bhroṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *kroṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*; *jhroṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*; *chroṃ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; and *jroṃ* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*; one should then place *oṃ namaḥ* at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).

Having performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*) as follows: *kroṃ* namaḥ on the command-finger; *bhroṃ* namaḥ on the mouth; *kroṃ* namaḥ on the throat; *jhroṃ* namaḥ on the heart; *chroṃ* namaḥ on the navel; *jroṃ* namaḥ on the *mūlādhāra*; *svāṃ* namaḥ on the right foot; and *hāṃ* namaḥ on the left foot.
Having performed the pervasion as before and meditated [on her] with "a body resembling molten gold" and so forth,

at the conclusion of the mental worship, one should— as before— draw two squares joined by four gates using saffron and other pigments on a plate of gold or similar material, and within that, an eight-petaled lotus.
Having drawn a circle within that, then an eight-sided figure (aṣṭāstra) within that, again a circle within that, then a hexagon (ṣaṭkoṇa) within that,
and again a circle within that; and having fashioned a womb (yoni) in its center with its apex facing oneself,
and having established it as before, one should proceed from the placement of the arghya and other offerings up to the end of the self-worship (ātmapūjā) as previously described.
Having worshipped the seat of Bhuvaneśvarī, and having performed the rites from the invocation (āvāhana) up to the installation of life-force (prāṇapratiṣṭhā), one should display the yoni-mudrā.

Then, after the offerings beginning with the seat (āsana) and ending with flowers, one should worship the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) as before around the Goddess within the yoni; [specifically] in the space between the yoni and the heart, on the part behind the Goddess.
Having worshipped the three rows of gurus as before, [one worships] on the two sides of the two squares:
"2 Brāhmīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ | 2 Māheśvarīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ |" On the two sides of the western door: "2 Kaumārīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ | 2 Vaiṣṇavīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ |"
Having worshipped with "Oṃ Vārāhī-pādukābhyāṃ namaḥ" and "Oṃ Indrāṇī-pādukābhyāṃ namaḥ" on the northern and southern sides of the eastern gate;
and with "Oṃ Cāmuṇḍā-pādukābhyāṃ namaḥ" and "Oṃ Mahālakṣmī-pādukābhyāṃ namaḥ" on the two sides of the southern gate;
then, in the northwest corner of the square, with "Oṃ Kṛtayuga-śakti-pādukābhyāṃ namaḥ," and in the northeast...

Having worshipped the descent of power (śaktipāta) of the Tretā Yuga in the southeast (āgneya), the descent of power of the Dvāpara Yuga in the southwest (nir-ṛti), and the descent of power of the Kali Yuga [in the northwest], then, within that, on the eight petals starting from the petal in front of the Goddess and proceeding clockwise: 2. Vijayā-pāda, 2. Vimalā-pāda, 2. Śubhā-pāda, 2. Viśvā-pāda.
Having worshipped with "vibhūtipāda," "vinatāpāda," "vividhāpāda," and "vimanāpāda," then,

within that [area], starting from the front of the Goddess and proceeding clockwise in the eight corners, one worships: "kamalāpāda," "kāminīpāda," "kirātīpāda," "kīrtipāda," "kurdinīpāda," and "kulasundarīpāda."
Having worshipped with "Kalyāṇī-pādukāyai" and "Kālakolā-pādukāyai," within that [mandala], in the six corners of the hexagon, worship the goddesses:

in the corner at the front-left, "Ḍākinī-pādukāyai"; in the corner at the front-right, "Rākiṇī-pādukāyai"; in the rear corner, "Lākinī-pādukāyai"; in the corner at the rear-left, "Kākinī-pādukāyai"; and in the rear-right corner, [worship Śākinī].
Having worshipped with "Śākinī-pādukāṃ" at the front corner of the Goddess and "Hākinī-pādukāṃ," then, in the triangle,
starting from the front corner of the Goddess and proceeding clockwise, [worship] with "Ichchhā-śakti-pādukāṃ," "Jñāna-śakti-pādukāṃ," and "Kriyā-śakti-pādukāṃ."

Having worshipped, one should designate four locations within the space between the eight-cornered and six-cornered [mandalas], starting from the right tip of the Goddess and ending at the right tip behind her, [reciting]: "Oṃ 2, obeisance to the arrows; Oṃ 2, obeisance to the sword; Oṃ 2, obeisance to the goad; Oṃ 2, obeisance to the noose."

Having worshipped the weapons situated from the lower right hand to the upper right hand of the deity, one should then conceive four positions starting from the back-left portion of the Goddess and extending to the front-left; in those [positions],
[one should worship] "Oṃ Gadayai Namaḥ" and "Oṃ Carmane Namaḥ."

Having worshipped with "Obeisance to Dhanus" and "Obeisance to Vajra," and having likewise worshipped the world-protectors (*lokapāla*) and their weapons as before, one should again [worship] the Nityā residing in the center.
Having worshipped that [deity] with the vidyā, one should conclude everything, including the incense and other offerings, as before; such is the procedure for the daily worship of Heruṇḍānityā.
Now follows the procedure for the daily worship of Vahnivāsinī Nityā. In the *Śrītantrarāja* (Chapter 11, Verse 1):
"Now, among the sixteen Nityās, she who was proclaimed as the sixth—that is the nine-syllabled Vidyā of Vahnivāsinī which has been described."
"The placement of the letters (*lipinyāsa*) on its limbs, meditation, and worship with the powers (*śakti*s).
Likewise, in that very same work (3rd Paṭala, verse 28): "Here, Bheruṇḍā and the others should come first, followed by Nityaklinnā and the others."
Then [the seed-syllables] Ambu (Vaṃ), Śūnya (Haṃ), Haṃsa-Agni-yuta-ambu (Raṃ), and Marut-yuta (Yaṃ). || 1 ||
The heart [HRĪM] joined with fire [RA], the void [Ū], joined with the pervasive [MA] and the pure [ŚA];
the void [Ū], joined with *namaḥ* [NA] and power [YĀ]: this nine-syllable mantra has thus been declared. (2)
"Everlasting, the bestower of all goals, dwelling in fire, the devourer of the universe.
Thus: *Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Vahnivāsinī*. In the Tripurārṇava:
"The seer is Vasiṣṭha, the meter is Gāyatrī, and this is the deity."
The seed-syllable and the power (śakti) constitute the beginning and the end, while the pin (kīlaka) is formed by the middle syllable.
Thus, in the *Tantrarāja* (11.3):
"One should join the long vowels with the second seed-syllable of the Vidyā;
one should perform the six limbs, ending with Māyā, upon one's own hands and limbs. (1)
One should place the nine syllables of the vidyā within the nine apertures; one should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpaka) with the entire mantra for the sake of the goddess’s self-perfection.
One should perform the pervasive ritual placement (nyāsa) in all branches of knowledge;
by that, the practitioner becomes identical with each of them, and through that, the accomplishments (siddhis) are attained.
And by the grace of the goddesses, these arise for him before long:
the six-limbed ritual of the Mātṛkā and the placement (nyāsa) of the Mātṛkā itself. (4)
Having first performed [the ritual] for all [the goddesses], one should subsequently place what has been taught therein;
that [placement] for Lalitā is said to be by means of exactly eight groups (vargas).
Therefore, the placement of her letters has not been described at all;
she resembles molten gold and is beautiful with fresh youth.
Her lotus-face was beautifully smiling, her three eyes were radiant,
she was endowed with eight arms, and she was resplendent with ornaments of rubies.
Her garment was reddened by the mingling rays of her ruby crown;
she wore yellow silk robes, with red anklets and a girdle.
Resplendent with ornaments of clusters interspersed with jewels and pearls,
she holds a red lotus, a conch, a *puṇḍra*, a sugarcane bow, and the orb of the full moon.
Holding a white lotus with a golden bud in her left arms,
and holding a flower and a citron in her right hands.
Having thus meditated upon Vahnavāsinī, who possesses a universal form and is surrounded on all sides by Śaktis identical to herself, one should worship her.
Javālinī, Visphuliṅginī, Maṅgalā, Sumanoharā, Kanakā, Kitavā, Viśvā, and Vividhā are the Śaktis. || 12 ||
One should worship [the deities] in the eight corners, starting from their tip and proceeding clockwise;
then, one should worship these twelve zodiacal powers (rāśi-śaktis) upon the petals.
By means of the names uttered within the midst of the seven-syllabled Māyā-mantra, she is called Ghasmarā,
Sarvabhakṣā, Viśvā, and Vividhodbhavā.
The tenth is proclaimed as Citrarūpā, who is free from calamity, free from fear, purifying, possessing inconceivable majesty, and red in color. 15.
She is proclaimed as Balidevī by means of the vidyās of Kurukullā and others;
wherever no deity is mentioned in the rite of bali-offering, there one should employ her.
One should fashion the deity of the bali offering as being endowed with the seven-syllable mantra;
having formed a nine-yoni diagram within two circles, one should draw a lotus outside of that.
One should fashion two circles joined by twelve petals;
outside of those, there should be two squares provided with two doors.
"In that wheel, one should likewise worship the Goddess in the east and west.

Now, the ritual application (*prayoga*): there, as before, having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the seat (*āsana*) and so forth up to the *yogapīṭha*, and having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the *Vahnivāsinī* mantra, [one should place] Vasiṣṭha as the seer (*ṛṣi*) upon the head.

Salutation! Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Salutation to the *gāyatrī* meter in the mouth; salutation to the eternal deity Vahnivāsinī in the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *oṃ hrīṃ* in the secret place; salutation to the power (*śakti*) of *namaḥ* in the feet; salutation to the *kīlaka* Vahnivāsinī in the navel," [one should say] "for me."

Having said, "This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the accomplishment of all desired goals," while joining the palms in reverence, one should perform the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the second seed-syllable conjoined with the six long vowels: *oṃ* namaḥ to the right eye;
*hrīṃ* namaḥ to the left; *vaṃ* namaḥ to the right ear.

Having performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*) with the root mantra, [reciting]: *hriṃ* namaḥ on the left nostril; *vāṃ* namaḥ on the right nostril; *siṃ* namaḥ on the left [nostril]; *nyaiṃ* namaḥ on the mouth; *naṃ* namaḥ on the *liṅga*; and *maṃḥ* namaḥ on the anus.

Having performed the pervasion (*vyāpaka*) and meditated [on the deity] beginning with "resembling molten gold" (*taptakāñcanasaṅkāśām*), and having completed the mental worship (*mānasapūjā*), one should draw a twelve-petaled lotus with saffron and other pigments upon a plate of gold or similar material; then, having fashioned two circles within its pericarp, in the center of those—

Having constructed the ninefold *yonicakra* as before, having fashioned two circles outside the lotus, and having made two squares outside those— each with a gateway on the east and west— one thus creates the worship-circle (*pūjācakra*).
Having installed it as before, worshipped it, and performed the rites from the placement of the *arghya* water up to the end of self-worship (*ātmapūjā*).
Having worshipped the seat of Bhuvaneśvarī as before, one should there fashion a form by means of the Vahnivāsinī-vidyā;

then, at the conclusion of the offerings such as invocation and so forth, having worshipped the six limbs as before in the space between the outer and inner circles, [one should worship] in the eight corners, starting from the front of the Goddess and proceeding clockwise. 2.
I worship Jvālinīpādukā, obeisance! 2 Visphuliṅginīpādukā; 2 Maṅgalāpādukā; 2 Manoharāpādukā; 2 Kanakāpādukā; 2 Kitavāpādukā; 2 Viśvāpādukā; 2 Vividhāpādukā.
Having thus worshipped, one should worship Meṣāpādukā on the twelve petals, starting from the front of the Goddess and proceeding clockwise.
I worship; obeisance! 2 Vṛṣāpāda... 2 Mithunāpāda... 2 Karkaṭāpāda... 2 Siṃhāpāda... 2 Kanyāpāda... 2 Tulāpāda... 2 Kīṭāpāda...
2 Cāpāpāda... 2 Makarāpāda... 2 Kumbhāpāda... Having worshipped with "Mīnāpāda" thus, [one worships] in the square.
Beginning from the southern side of the main gate of the Goddess and proceeding clockwise, one should worship [the goddesses] Dyasmarāpā,
Sarvabhakṣāpā, Viśvāpā, Vividhodbhavāpā, and Citrarūpāpā in the two flanks of the western door, as well as in the northwest, north, and northeast.

Having worshipped [the goddesses] with "I worship Niḥsapatnāpādukā, obeisance! and likewise "Nirātaṅkāpādukā," "Pāvanīpādukā," "Acintyavaibhavāpādukā," and "Raktāpādukā" in the two flanks— the northern and southern— of the eastern gate, as well as in the southeast, south, and southwest corners, one should worship outside of that.

Then, having worshipped the world-protectors (lokapālas) and the weapons as before, one should complete everything—including incense, lamps, and so forth—as previously described; this is the procedure for the daily worship of Vahnivāsinī Nityā.
Now follows the procedure for the worship of Vajreśvarīnityā. Regarding this, the Śrītantrarāja states (12th Paṭala):
"Now, among the sixteen Nityās, that which is proclaimed as the seventh—I shall describe its ritual procedure, which accomplishes all aims; listen! (1)
The Vidyā consisting of twelve syllables has already been declared previously;
now [follow] its limbs, the ritual placement of the letters (lipinyāsa), the meditation, and the worship with the Śaktis.
Thus:
(3.41) "The second [syllable] of Vahnivāsinī, the fourth of Nityaklinnā, the first of Bhagamālā, and the second of Bheruṇḍā. (1)
The second is *nityaklinnā*, the third and sixth-seventh are [the next two], and the eighth and ninth; this is declared to be the first group.

"The eternal Mahāvajreśvarī is proclaimed as having twelve syllables. Thus: *hrīṃ klinne aiṃ kroṃ nityamadadrave hrīṃ*. In the *Tripurārṇava*, Brahmā is celebrated as the seer (*ṛṣi*). The *gāyatrī* meter is declared [to be the meter], and the deity is the Supreme Goddess (*parameśvarī*). The Supreme Goddess.
"Vajreśvarī; at the beginning and end are the Seed and the Power, while the Vāgbhava syllable is the Kilaka. Thus it is said in the *Tantrarāja* (12.4):
"In this [system], there are two, one, and also two, two, and then two."
Having enveloped [the deity] with Māyā, one should perform the six limbs in their proper sequence.
(One should perform the placement with each of the ten mantras encased by the *Śakti* mantra:
sequentially upon the eyes, ears, nose, speech, chest, navel, and the private parts. (2)
Red in color, clad in red garments, adorned with red perfumes, garlands, and ornaments,
she has four arms and three eyes, and is radiant with a crown of rubies.
She holds in her arms a noose, a goad, a bow made of sugarcane, and likewise a pomegranate as an arrow,
with eyes cooled by compassion and joy.
Beholding the practitioner within the city of the earth, [the lotus] with three triangles, six corners, and a lotus,
she sits comfortably in the center of the wheel, her lotus-face smiling.
She is surrounded by Śaktis who are her own essential forms and stands in the center of a boat;
she is also surrounded by Śaktis situated on a throne and on a swaying boat nearby.
One should meditate upon the Mistress of Mantras in the ocean of the dawn-red sky, constantly surrounded by those [attendants] and engaged in diversions such as coming and going.
There, the powers of will, knowledge, and action reside in the triangle;
the Ḍākinīs and others reside in the hexagon, situated upon the twelve petals of the lotus.
Hṛllekhā, Kledinī, Klinnā, Kṣobhiṇī, Madanāturā, Nirañjanā, Rāgavatī, and likewise Madanāvatī. || 9 ||
Mekhalā, Drāviṇī, and Vegavatī are the twelve Śaktis.
Thereafter, O Ambikā, listen to the Śaktis residing upon the sixteen petals.
To Kamalā, Kāminī, Kalpā, and Kalā, who are filled with wonder; to Kirātā, who destroys the darkness of time; to Kauśikī, who bears a conch shell—[I bow]. (11)
Listen now in due order to Kātarā, Kapaṭā, Kīrti, Kumārī, and Kuṅkumā, as well as to the Śaktis who abide in the four corners.
She is the breaker, the swift, the one possessing enjoyments, the fickle, the clever, the virtuous, delight, faith, the one craving enjoyment, the intoxicated with pride, and the high-minded. 13.
One should worship these twelve great goddesses situated in the cardinal directions, the gates, the sides, and the corners, surrounding the square on all sides.
Having offered the *arghya* with the *aṅga* and *mūla* mantras, one should then worship [the deity] in the form described;
thereafter, one should worship the red ocean, the golden boat, and the lion-throne.
There, having invoked the Goddess into the wheel as before, one should worship her with the powers (śaktis) using names situated within the seven-syllable Māyā-mantra.
Thereafter, one should offer the bali-oblation with the previously mentioned seven-syllable mantra,
and perform the fire sacrifice (homa) for the goddess Kurukullā according to the prescribed rite.
One should perform the fire-oblation (homa) with reddish flowers smeared with ghee, or with ghee alone; one should conclude it as previously described. Thus has your worship been explained.

Thus [ends the section]. Now, the ritual application (*prayoga*): there, as before, having performed the worship of the seat (*āsana-pūjā*) and so forth up to the end of the placement on the *yogapīṭha*, one should perform three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the root mantra. Then: "Salutation to Brahmā, the seer (*ṛṣi*), upon the head;
salutation to the Gāyatrī meter (*chandas*), upon the mouth; salutation to the deity Vajreśvarī Nityā, upon the heart."

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) thus: "Salutation to the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* in the secret place; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *hrīṃ* in the two feet; salutation to the pin (*kīlaka*) *aiṃ* in the navel," and having said with palms joined, "The application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of all my desired goals," [one recites]: "To *hrīṃ klinne*, salutation to the heart; *aiṃ*, svāhā to the head; *kroṃ*..."
"Vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Huṃ to the eternal armor (kavaca). Vauṣaṭ to the three eyes of intoxication (mada-netratraya).
Phaṭ to the weapon (astra) of the fluid Hrīṃ. Having thus performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the six limbs upon the hands, [one places]:
"Hrīṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to the right eye; Hrīṃ Nneṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to the left eye; [Hrīṃ] to the right ear..."

*Hrīṃ-aiṃ-hrīṃ*, obeisance! At the left ear: *hrīṃ-kroṃ-hrīṃ*, obeisance! At the right nostril: *hrīṃ-trīṃ-hrīṃ*, obeisance! At the left nostril: *hrīṃ-tyaṃ-hrīṃ*, obeisance! At the mouth: *hrīṃ-maṃ-hrīṃ*, obeisance! At the chest: *hrīṃ-daṃ-hrīṃ*, obeisance! At the navel...
Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with "Hrīṃ indraṃ hrīṃ, obeisance" [on the head] and "Hrīṃ veṃ hrīṃ, obeisance" on the *liṅga*,
and having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) with the root mantra, one should meditate upon her as "clad in white and red garments," and so forth.
Having performed the mental worship (*mānasapūjā*), one should [draw the seat] as before on a pedestal made of gold or other materials using saffron and the like.
Having fashioned a yoni in the form of a triangle with its apex facing oneself,
one should construct outside of that a twelve-petaled lotus, outside of that a sixteen-petaled lotus,
and outside of that two squares provided with four gates; thus, having prepared the worship mandala.

Having established [the deity] before oneself as before and worshipped [her], from the placement of the *arghya* vessel up to the end of the self-worship (*ātmapūjā*), one should worship the pedestal (*pīṭha*) of Bhuvaneśvarī by worshipping [the sequence] from Maṇḍūka to Earth; thereafter:
"Obeisance to the Crimson Ocean (*śoṇasamudra*); obeisance to the Golden Boat (*kanakapotā*); obeisance to the Jewel Throne (*ratnasiṃhāsana*)."

Having thus worshipped, and thereafter having worshipped the pedestal (pīṭha) beginning with Dharma and ending with Manu as before, one should there fashion the form (mūrti) by means of the root-mantra (mūlavidyā) and serve it with the ritual offerings (upacāra) beginning with invocation (āvāhana) and ending with flowers;
then, having worshipped the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) in the middle of the triangle as before, [one worships] the Goddess in the space between the two triangles.

Having worshipped the three rows of gurus on the back as before, one should worship within the inner triangle, proceeding clockwise starting from the front of the Goddess: *hrīṃ hṛllekhāpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*,
*hrīṃ kledinīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*, *hrīṃ klinnāpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*, *hrīṃ kṣobhiṇīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*.

Hraum Madanāpā0 | Hrīm Madanāturāpā0 | Hrīm Nirañjanāpā0 | Hrīm Rāgavatīpā0 | Hrīm Madanāvatīpā0 | Hrīm Mekhalāpā0 | Hrīm Drāviṇīpā0 | Hrīm Vegavatīpā0. Having thus worshipped, [worship] outside of that.
Upon the sixteen petals [of the lotus] are: Kamalāpā, Kāminīpā, Kalpāpā, Kalāpā, Kalitāpā, Kautukāpā, Kirātāpā, Kālāpā, Kadanāpā, Kauśikīpā,
Kambuvāhinīpā, Kātarāpā, Kapaṭāpā, Kīrtipā, and Kumārīpā.

Having worshipped with *kuṅkumāpā* and so forth as before, one should worship on the sides of the four gates of the square, starting from the front of the Goddess and proceeding clockwise from the southern side of the western gate:
*Bhañjinīpā*, *Veginīpā*, *Bhogāpā*, *Capalāpā*, *Peśalāpā*, and *Satīpā*.

Having worshipped [the goddesses] as "Ratipā," "Śraddhāpā," and "Prītipā," one should worship, in the four corners starting from the northwest (vāyavya) in clockwise order as before, "Bhogalolāpā," "Madanāpā," "Unmattāpā," and "Manasvinīpā," ending in the southwest (nir-ṛti). Then, as before, perform the worship of the world-protectors (lokapāla) and so forth for the remainder.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the daily worship of Vajreśvarī Nityā.
Now follows the procedure for the worship of the Nityā Śivādūtī. In that regard, the *Śrītantrarāja* (13th Paṭala) states:
"Now, among the sixteen Nityās, she who is declared as the eighth—listen, O wise one, to her ritual procedure which bestows the desired fruit. (1)

The extraction of the mantra was performed previously; now, likewise, [I shall describe] the sequence of ritual placement (nyāsa), as well as the surrounding powers (āvaraṇa-śakti), its meditation, and its worship.
Thus it is said. In that very same [text], at 3.44:
"Vajreśvarī is the last and the first; then there is ether joined with fire.
Water should be joined with wind, and then the mountain (gotrā) joined with earth. (1)
Immediately after that, there should be the letter *ra* conjoined with the pervasive (*vyāpaka*) and the pure (*śuci*).
The two final vowels [ū and ṛ] are declared to be the messenger (*dūtī*), the eternal (*nityā*) goddess Vahnivāsinī. (2)

p. 299) Thus: *hrīṃ śivādūtyai namaḥ*. In the *Tripurārṇava*: "The seer is Rudra, the meter is Gāyatrī, and the deity is Śivā; [the mantra is] 'Śivādūtī'. The seed-syllable (*bīja*) and power (*śakti*) are at the beginning and end, and the middle is..."
Thus the *kīlaka* is described. In the *Śrītantrarāja* (13.5):

"Having performed the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) as before according to the stated path beginning with the Vidyā, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) upon the five [senses] beginning with hearing using the syllables encased by that very [Vidyā]. (1)
Having placed the sixth [syllable] upon the mind, one should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpakanyāsa) with the Vidyā.
The arghya is prescribed as before; now hear, O Pārvatī, about its powers.
Vihvalā, Ākarṣiṇī, Lolā, Nityā, Vanamālinī, Madanamālinī, Vinodā, Kautukā, Puṇyā, Purāṇā, and Caturasragā— (3).
"Vāgīśī, Varadā, Viśvā, Vinadā, Vighnakāriṇī,
Vīrā, Vighnaharā, and Vidyā"— having spoken thus, these are the eight powers of the yantra.
Sumukhī, Sundarī, Sārā, Sumanā, Sarasvatī, Samayā, Sarvagā, and Vidyā— these are said to be the eight Aṣṭāstra-Śaktis.
The Ḍākinīs and the others [are located] in the six hexagons, all starting from the front and proceeding clockwise;
they are endowed with forms, colors, and weapons identical to those of the Root Goddess.
One should worship all around on the six petals Śivā, Vāṇī, Dūrasiddhā, Tyai, Vigrahavatī, Nādā, and Manonmanī.
One should worship the powers of will, knowledge, and action in the three corners;
in the center, one should worship the eighth goddess, Śivā, who is surrounded by weapons.
O wise one, listen to her meditation, of which this entire universe is said to consist;
nevertheless, she has assumed a supreme form for the sake of destroying all the afflictions of her devotees.
She possesses a radiance equal to the midday sun at the time of its setting,
wears a crown of nine jewels, has three eyes, and is clad in crimson garments.
Her body’s luster was resplendent, enhanced by various ornaments;
she possessed a pure smile, had eight arms, and was being praised by great sages.
With his left arms he holds a noose, a shield, a mace, and a jeweled goblet; likewise, with his right hands, he holds a goad, a sword, an axe, and a lotus.
Having thus meditated upon the Goddess—the messenger who destroys misconduct, who is endowed with the exertion to grant the desires of practitioners—one should worship her. (13)
Two circles, an exterior triangle, and those two [forming] a six-petaled lotus;
likewise, a hexagon, an octagon, and that [forming] an eight-petaled lotus. (14)
Having drawn the Fire-Dweller (Vahni-vāsinī) within the Bhūpura (the outer square), one should invoke Śivā situated in its center,
worship her, and then worship her powers established according to the previously mentioned procedure.
"Having recited [the mantra], having offered oblations, and having paid obeisance, one should likewise dissolve [the deity] into one's own self.

Thus [it is said]. Now, the ritual application (*prayoga*): there, as before, after the worship of the seat (*āsana-pūjā*) and so forth up to the end of the placement of the *yogapīṭha*, one should perform three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the root-mantra (*mūla*). Then, on the head: "Obeisance to Rudra, the seer (*ṛṣi*); on the mouth..."

Salutation to the Gāyatrī metre. Salutation to the eternal Śrīśivādūtī at the heart. Salutation to the seed-syllable Hrīṃ at the secret place. Salutation to the power (Śakti) of the word "namas" at the feet. Having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa), saying "Salutation to Śivādūtī, the bolt (kīlaka), at the navel," one declares: "This is the application for the attainment of my desired goal."

Having spoken with palms joined in reverence and performed the *kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa* (the ritual assignment of mantras to the hands and six limbs) beginning with *hrāṃ hrīṃ*, etc., [one should assign]:
*hrīṃ śiṃ hrīṃ namaḥ* to the two ears; *hrīṃ vāṃ hrīṃ namaḥ* to the entire body;
*hrīṃ dūṃ hrīṃ namaḥ* to the two eyes; and *hrīṃ tyaiṃ hrīṃ namaḥ* to the tongue.

Having performed the pervasive application (*vyāpaka*) with the entire mantra beginning with "To the two nostrils: *hrīṃ naṃ hrīṃ* namaḥ" and "To the mind: *hrīṃ maṃ hrīṃ* namaḥ," and having meditated according to the [verse] beginning with "In the season of heat...
and performed the mental worship (*mānasapūjā*) as before, [one should draw the diagram] on a plate of gold or other materials with saffron and so forth.

Having fashioned a six-petalled lotus, within it a circle (or two circles), in the center a triangle with its apex facing oneself (and within that two circles), outside the lotus a hexagon, outside that an octagon, outside that an eight-petalled lotus, and outside that—

Having constructed a square worship-circle (pūjācakra) provided with gates in the east and west, one should place it before oneself as previously described; having worshipped it and performed the rites beginning with the placement of the arghya water up to the end of self-worship,
one should mentally project the form (mūrti) by means of the root mantra, and after the offerings from invocation through the presentation of flowers, [perform the rites] within the triangle.

Having worshipped the six limbs as before, and having worshipped the three lines of Gurus within the space between the triangle and the circle as before, one should worship [the goddesses] in the square, starting from the right side of the door facing the Goddess and proceeding clockwise: *Oṃ Vihvalāpādu*, *Ākarṣiṇīpā*.

Having worshipped Lolāpā, Nityāpā, Madanāpā, Mālinīpā, Vinodāpā, Kautukāpā, Puṇyāpā, and Purāṇāpā, one should worship Vāgīśīpā, Varadāpā, Viśvāpā, Vinadāpā, Vighnakāriṇīpā, and Vīrāpā upon the eight petals as before.

Having worshipped with "vighnaharāyai pādukāṃ" and "vidyāyai pādukāṃ," one should worship as before in the eight corners with "sumukhyai pādukāṃ," "sundaryai pādukāṃ," "sārāyai pādukāṃ," "sumanāyai pādukāṃ," "sarasvatyai pādukāṃ," "samayāyai pādukāṃ," "sarvagāyai pādukāṃ," and "siddhāyai pādukāṃ. Then, in the six corners, beginning from the corner at the front of the Goddess, [one worships] "hākinīyai pādukāṃ."
Having worshipped Śākinī-pāda, Kākinī-pāda, Lākinī-pāda, Rākiṇī-pāda, and Ḍākinī-pāda,
one should worship on the six petals Śivā-pāda, Vāṇī-pāda, Dūrasiddhā-pāda, Tyai-vigrahavatī-pāda, Nādā-pāda, and Manonmanī-pāda; then, within the inner triangles—

Having worshipped [the goddesses] by proceeding clockwise from the tip of the Goddess, namely: *icchāśaktipāda*, *jñānaśaktipāda*, and *kriyāśaktipāda*, one should then imagine the locations of the weapons, starting from the lower right hand of the Goddess and ending with the lower left hand, in the space between the inner circle and the triangle.
Salutation to Kamala.
300) Salutation to the axe. Salutation to the sword. Salutation to the goad. Salutation to the jeweled goblet.

*Namaḥ*. *Namaḥ* to the mace (*gadā*). *Namaḥ* to the shield (*kheṭa*). *Namaḥ* to the noose (*pāśa*). Having thus worshipped [the attendants], one should again worship the Goddess in the center and conclude everything, including the incense, lamps, and so forth, as previously described.
This is the procedure for the daily worship of the Nityā Śivādūtī.
Now, the procedure for the constant worship of Tvaritā. In the *Śrītantrarāja* (14th Patala):
"Now, among the sixteen Nityās, that which is proclaimed as the ninth is indeed the Vidyā Tvaritā, previously described as having twelve syllables. (1)

O wise one, listen to the procedure for that, together with the fire-oblation, the yantra, and so forth, by which the practitioner of mantra, radiant as the god of love, agitates the surface of the earth. (2)
Thus it is said. In that very same place (3.47):
"The first [syllable] belongs to Vahnivāsinī; immediately after that are the messenger (dūtī) and so forth;
the Haṃsa is conjoined with the sister of the Earth (Dharā), together with the moving fire (Tejaścara). || 1 ||
Vāyu (ya), joined with Prabhācara (ra); Grāsa (kṣa) endowed with Śakti (ī); Hṛt (ha), Raya (ra), and Dāha (ra)—O Dear One, these constitute the eighth [syllable], Vahni (hra). || 2 ||
The *haṃsa* joined with *kṣmā* is the *grāsa*; joined with *cara*, it is the second.
*Dyuti* joined with *nāda* is the eternal *tvaritā* consisting of twelve syllables. (3)
Thus: *oṃ hrīṃ huṃ khe cha kṣaḥ strī hūṃ kṣe hrīṃ phaṭ*. Likewise, in the *Tripurārṇava*:
"O Pārvatī, Sauri is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Virāṭ is the meter (*chanda*), and this [goddess] is the deity (*devatā*).
'Strī' is said to be the armor (*kavaca*), 'śakti' the seed-syllable (*bīja*), and 'kṣe' the pin (*kīlaka*). (1)
This [mantra], however, is the eternal *Tvaritā*. As stated in the *Tantrajāla* (14.3):
"One should perform the six limbs for the hands and the body respectively, using the seven syllables beginning with the fourth letter of the Vidyā, in pairs."
In the head, forehead, and throat; in the heart, navel, and foundation (ādhāra);
likewise in the pair of thighs, the pair of knees, and the pair of shanks.
Likewise, one should place ten syllables born of the mantra upon the pair of feet;
these are formed by the remaining mantra-syllables situated in the second, penultimate, and middle positions.
Listen to the meditation on Tārā and others, their powers, and their worship:
she is dark-complexioned, of auspicious form, and radiant with fresh youth. (4)
Resplendent with ornaments fashioned from eight nāgas arranged in pairs—
namely, earrings, armlets, and likewise a girdle accompanied by anklets— (5)
She was clothed in garments of fresh sprouts by those of the Brahmin, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra castes, who possessed formidable forms, and adorned with beautiful crests made of peacock feathers.
Her arms were adorned with bracelets, she was radiant with a crown of rubies, she wore a crest made of peacock feathers, and she possessed that very umbrella and those very banners.
Her chest was adorned with the saffron of her breasts, shimmering with strings of *guñjā* berries; she possessed three eyes, a beautiful face, and a lotus-like countenance with a gentle smile.

Having thus meditated upon the goddess Totulā, who possesses four shimmering arms holding a noose, a goad, the gesture of granting boons, and the gesture of fearlessness, one should worship her as she is surrounded by her Śaktis.
And at her forefront stood Phaṭkārī, radiant with bow and arrow in hand,
intent upon bestowing grace and granting fruits to the practitioners with great haste.
Since she was called "The Swift One" by me, she is this ninth Śakti;
she is black in complexion, holds a mace in her hand, and has curly hair standing upright on her head.
The servant (Kiṅkara) is to be worshipped before her for the accomplishment of all goals;
on both sides of her door, those known as Jaya and Vijaya are to be worshipped.
The two Śaktis, Huṃkārī and Khecarī, who resemble her and hold golden canes in their lotus-like hands, are followed by Caṇḍā, Chedinī, and Kṣepiṇī. (13)
Strī and Huṃkāryā, along with these Kṣemakarīs who are equal to the world-protectors—
these powers of the mantra-syllables, stationed upon the eight petals of the lotus, are to be worshipped.
O Maheśvarī, hear now the procedure for the worship of that Ārdrā (Tvaritā), by whose constant adoration a man becomes like the god of love among women. (15)
Having prepared the *arghya* as before, one should arrange two *bhūpura*s upon an auspicious golden throne supported by eight lion-claws for the Goddess.
Having fashioned a pair of circles within that [mandala] joined with a western gate,
and an eight-petaled lotus within those [circles], one should [place] the supreme Śivā there.
Having invoked her as before, surrounded by the Śaktis,
one should worship her as prescribed, preceded by the display of the mudrās.
The two previously mentioned [deities] are to be worshipped either at the tip of the foremost leaf or in the middle of the circle;
one should offer the bali-oblation for Kiṅkara before the Goddess with the mantras previously recited.
Having thus performed worship with devotion before one who stands within a maṇḍala crowded with members of his own group, he should recite the vidyā one thousand times.
"Or, having performed one hundred *homas*, he should complete the worship as before.

Thus [ends the section]. Now, the ritual procedure (*prayoga*): there, having performed the placement of the seat (*āsana*) and so forth up to the *yogapīṭha-nyāsa* as before, and having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the *Tvaritā* mantra, he should place: "Salutation to the sage Saura on the head."
p.
301) Salutation to the Virāṭ meter in the mouth; salutation to the deity Tvaritā-nityā in the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable Oṃ in the secret place;
salutation to the Śakti Huṃ at the feet; [salutation] to the Kīlaka Kṣe at the navel.
Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with "Oṃ *namaḥ*," and having said with palms joined, "This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the attainment of my desired goal," [one recites]:
Oṃ *kh* to the heart, *namaḥ*. *Cha* *c* to the head, *svāhā*. *Che* *kṣaḥ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*.
*Kṣaḥ* *strī* to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*. *Strī* *hūṃ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*. *Hūṃ* *kṣe* to the weapon (*astra*).
Having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) with the syllable *phaṭ*, [one should place]: *hrīṃ oṃ hrīṃ namaḥ* on the head;
*hrīṃ huṃ hrīṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *hrīṃ khe hrīṃ namaḥ* on the throat;
*hrīṃ ca hrīṃ namaḥ* on the heart; *hrīṃ che hrīṃ namaḥ* on the navel; and [the same] on the *mūlādhāra*.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the syllables encapsulated by *Māyā* (the *Hrīṃ*) as follows: *hrīṃ kṣaḥ hrīṃ namaḥ* on the two thighs; *hrīṃ strīṃ hrīṃ namaḥ* on the two knees; *hrīṃ hūṃ hrīṃ namaḥ* on the two shanks; *hrīṃ kṣeh hrīṃ namaḥ* on the two calves; and *hrīṃ phaṭ hrīṃ namaḥ* on the two feet—[one should then perform it] with the entire *Vidyā*.

Having performed the mental worship beginning with meditation after having arranged the pervasive [deity], one should construct the worship-circle (pūjācakra) by first drawing two squares with doors on the west and so forth using saffron and other pigments upon a gold plate or similar surface, and within that, an eight-petaled lotus provided with two concentric circles.
Having established [the deity] in front as before and worshipped it, and having performed the rites from the placement of the *arghya* vessel up to the end of self-worship (*ātmapūjā*),

Having worshipped the three rows of gurus, one should thereafter [place] the sandals of Phaṭkārī at the outer edge of the two paths within the three outer circles, outside the tip of the petal in front of the Goddess. On the eight petals, having worshipped with *huṃkārapā*, *khecarīpā*, *caṇḍā*, *chedinīpā*, *kṣepiṇīpā*, *strīkārīpā*, *hūṃkārīpā*, and *kṣemakarīpā*, one should complete everything, including the worship of the world-protectors (*lokapāla*) and so forth, as previously described. Here...
After the offering of the bali to Kurukullā, one should also present a bali of food and other items before the Goddess for Kiṅkara; such is the procedure for the daily worship of Tvaritā.

A rosary of coral beads, a lotus, a water-pot fashioned from jewels, a cup filled with gems, a loincloth, and the seal-ring of exposition. || 10 ||
Holding in her right and left hands a book and a beautiful red lotus, and in [other] arms a golden pen, a jeweled necklace, and an excellent conch shell. (11)

Having meditated thus, one should worship her constantly for the sake of attaining eloquence, fortune, and a beloved;

Speech is Sarasvatī, the voice, whether refined (Sanskrit) or other (Prakrit);
she is multiform and of wondrous form, delightful and full of joy and playfulness. 15.
Thus, eleven [deities] have been proclaimed; one should worship them within the nine wombs (navayoni).

In the square, one should worship the world-protectors in the form of spears:
Indra, Agni, Yama, Rakṣas, Varuṇa, Anila, Soma, and Kubera.

For the sake of all accomplishments, one should worship Īśa, Ananta, and Vidhi in the eight directions starting from the east, arranged from bottom to top, using their names ending with "Śakti" as before.
One should construct two squares joined by gates facing east and west; in their center, one should fashion an eight-petaled lotus situated within a pair of circles.
Having divided [the area] into four, three, five, and four parts, thus forming nine compartments, one should then duly invoke her there and worship her correctly as before.
One should worship the eleven internal powers on both sides of the central womb;

O Ambikā, this very [practice] is the general mode of worship;

Then, on the head: "Salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the seer (*ṛṣi*); on the mouth..."

Salutation to Paṅktichandas. Salutation to the deity Kulasundarīnityā in the heart. Salutation to the seed-syllable Aiṃ in the secret place. Salutation to the Śakti Sauḥ in the feet. Having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) with "Salutation to the Kīlaka Klīṃ in the navel," [one declares]: "The application is for the attainment of my fourfold human goals."

Having spoken with palms joined at the commencement of the worship and the commencement of the recitation, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the hands and limbs as follows: *Āṃ* to the heart, *Namaḥ*; *Īṃ* to the head, *Svāhā*; *Ūṃ* to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*), *Vaṣaṭ*; *Aiṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *Huṃ*; *Auṃ* to the three eyes, *Vauṣaṭ*; *Aḥ* to the weapon (*astra*), *Phaṭ*. Then, [placing *Aiṃ*] upon the head...

Āṃ, salutation to the upward-facing face. At the mouth: Aiṃ īṃ, salutation to the eastern face. At the right ear: Aiṃ ūṃ, salutation to the southern face. At the left ear: Aiṃ aiṃ, salutation to the northern face. Below the crest-lock: Aiṃ auṃ, salutation to the western face.

One should perform the placement (nyāsa) on the chin with: *aiṃ aḥ aparavaktrāya namaḥ*. In the midst of the worship, at the commencement of the worship of the enclosures (*āvaraṇa-pūjā*), one should take the middle seed-syllable of the Vidyā, divide it by the six long vowels, and perform the placement starting with *klāṃ klīm*, and so forth. At the end of the worship as well, [one should place] the final seed-syllable of the Vidyā.
In the same manner, having modified the vowel, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) with "Sāṃ Sīm" and so forth, both in the center and during the recitation (*japa*).

"During the recitation" means after half of the prescribed number of recitations has been completed. Now, in the present context, after the placement of the faces of the first *kūṭa*, [one who] is [the practitioner] should place "Aiṃ" in the *ādhāra*.

*klīṃ* at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*); *sauḥ* at the heart; *aiṃ* at the right eye; *klīṃ* at the left eye; *sauḥ* at the eye on the forehead; *aiṃ* at the right ear; *klīṃ* at the left; *sauḥ* at the chin;

Sauḥ. At the base of the right arm: Aiṃ; in the middle: Klīṃ; at the tip: Sauḥ. At the base of the left arm: Aiṃ; in the middle: Klīṃ; at the tip: Sauḥ. At the base of the right thigh: Aiṃ; in the middle: Klīṃ; at the tip: Sauḥ. At the base of the left thigh: Aiṃ; in the middle: Klīṃ; at the tip: Sauḥ. Thus, it is likewise for both hands and feet.

Having performed the placement [of the mantras] in that manner, one should then perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) by means of the root-vidyā. Furthermore, during both the middle and the end of the worship and recitation,

The Tradition: Then, at the conclusion of the mental worship consisting of meditation, one should draw an eight-petaled lotus with saffron and other pigments on a plate of gold or similar material as before.
Having fashioned the nine-yoni wheel within its pericarp as previously described, one should draw two circles outside the lotus, and beyond those—
Having constructed the worship mandala by forming two squares joined at their eastern and western gates,
one should place it before oneself as previously described, perform worship, set out the arghya and other offerings, and complete the self-worship.
After performing the worship up to the pedestal (pīṭhapūjā) as before, ending with the cognition of the frog and so forth,
one should offer salutations to Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, Ambikā, Icchā, Jñānā, Kriyā, Kulikā, and Citrā upon the filaments of the eight-petaled lotus.

Having worshipped the twelve Śaktis— Viṣadhnyai, Dūtaryai, Ānandāyai, and so forth— and having worshipped the entire pedestal with the mantra *hasauṃ sadāśivamahāpretapadmāsanāya namaḥ*, one should there fashion the form by means of the Kulasundarī-vidyā, and perform the rites beginning with invocation (*āvāhana*) up to the installation of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*).

Having worshipped the six faces of the Goddess with the previously mentioned mantras for the placement (*nyāsa*) of the six faces, and having completed the ritual services beginning with the seat (*āsana*), one should then worship the front corner of the triangle with "2 Bhāṣāpā" (Obeisance to Bhāṣā).
Then, in the eight triangles, starting from the front triangle of the Goddess and proceeding clockwise, one should worship with "2 Sarasvatīpā" (Obeisance to Sarasvatī).

Having worshipped the eight Śaktis— Vāṇīpā, Saṃskṛtāpā, Prākṛtāpā, Parāpā, Bahurūpāpā, Citrarūpāpā, and Ramyāpā— one should worship Ānandāpā in the right-rear corner of the inner-yoni of the Goddess, and Kautukāpā to her left.

Having worshipped [the goddesses] on the eight petals as before— namely Brāhmī and the others— and having worshipped the world-protectors (lokapālas) on the square as before, beginning with "Indra-Śakti-pādukāṃ" and so forth, worshipping them in the form of Śaktis,
and likewise worshipping their weapons also in the form of Śaktis, one should perform all the rites beginning with incense (dhūpa).
One should conclude as before; this is the ritual procedure for the daily worship of Kulasundarīnityā.

hear from me as I describe the infinite powers of the Goddess.

Salutation to the Seer (Ṛṣi). Salutation to the Paṅkti metre in the mouth. Salutation to the deity Nityānityā in the heart.

Having spoken with palms joined: *hsāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *hsīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *hsūṃ* to the tuft of hair, *vaṣaṭ*; *hsaiṃ* to the armor, *huṃ*; *hsauṃ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; *hsaḥ* to the weapon, *phaṭ*. Having drawn a hexagon with saffron and other pigments on a plate of gold or similar material, and having made a circle in its center, one should draw thirty-six lotuses outside the hexagon— either each possessing sixteen petals,

Having divided that [space] externally, one should construct two outer squares provided with four gates; thus, having fashioned the worship maṇḍala, one should place it before oneself as previously described, perform worship, arrange the arghya and other offerings, and so forth, up to the end of self-worship.

Having worshipped the Kulasundarī-pīṭha with the root mantra and having mentally fashioned the form [of the deity], one should invoke [the deity] and perform the rites beginning with the seat up to the offering of flowers. Having worshipped the three rows [of deities], [one offers] at the southwest corner (nir-ṛtikoṇa): 2 Ḍākinī-pāda; at the northwest corner (vāyavya): 2 Rākiṇī-pāda; at the eastern corner: 2.

In this way, one should worship the thirty-five (or thirty-six) phoneme-energies (*varṇaśakti*) in the other [lotuses] as well— namely, sixteen energies per lotus— according to the previously mentioned phoneme-energies of the full mandala.
However, in the case of eighteen lotuses, there are thirty-two [energies] per lotus.

The aforementioned Śaktis are to be worshipped. Now, having fashioned outside the hexagon a lotus consisting of fifty-one petals, one should worship the fifty-one Śaktis of the phonemes upon those petals, starting from the front of the Goddess and proceeding clockwise. As follows:

Having fashioned a set of six lotuses— outside the hexagon a sixteen-petaled lotus, outside that a twelve-petaled one, outside that a ten-petaled one, outside that a six-petaled one, outside that a four-petaled one, and outside that a two-petaled one— one should [place] upon those sixteen petals...

One should contemplate the fifty powers: the powers of the vowels in the twelve petals, the powers of the consonants from *ka* to *ṭha* in the ten petals, the powers of the consonants from *ḍa* to *pha* in the six petals, the powers of the consonants from *va* to *la* in the four petals, and the powers of the letters *ha* and *kṣa* in the two petals.

The eighth and ninth [syllables] are those situated below the penultimate [letter], immediately following the blue banner (nīlapatākā),
as well as the final syllable of Tvaritā and Bheruṇḍā.
"This Jvālāmālā [mantra], consisting of sixty-three syllables, is said to be eternal.
